## Bulk set issue property

<a id="opIdbulkSetIssueProperty"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issue/properties/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "filter": {
      "currentValue": {
        "owner": "admin",
        "weight": 50
      },
      "entityIds": [
        10100,
        100010
      ],
      "hasProperty": true
    },
    "value": {
      "owner": "admin",
      "weight": 100
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/issue/properties/{propertyKey}`

Sets a property value on multiple issues.

The value set can be a constant or determined by a [Jira expression](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/jira-expressions/). Expressions must be computable with constant complexity when applied to a set of issues. Expressions must also comply with the [restrictions](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/jira-expressions/#restrictions) that apply to all Jira expressions.

The issues to be updated can be specified by a filter.

The filter identifies issues eligible for update using these criteria:

 *  `entityIds` Only issues from this list are eligible.
 *  `currentValue` Only issues with the property set to this value are eligible.
 *  `hasProperty`:
    
     *  If *true*, only issues with the property are eligible.
     *  If *false*, only issues without the property are eligible.

If more than one criteria is specified, they are joined with the logical *AND*: only issues that satisfy all criteria are eligible.

If an invalid combination of criteria is provided, an error is returned. For example, specifying a `currentValue` and `hasProperty` as *false* would not match any issues (because without the property the property cannot have a value).

The filter is optional. Without the filter all the issues visible to the user and where the user has the EDIT\_ISSUES permission for the issue are considered eligible.

This operation is:

 *  transactional, either all eligible issues are updated or, when errors occur, none are updated.
 *  [asynchronous](#async). Follow the `location` link in the response to determine the status of the task and use [Get task](#api-rest-api-3-task-taskId-get) to obtain subsequent updates.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for each project containing issues.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
 *  *Edit issues* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for each issue.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "filter": {
    "currentValue": {
      "owner": "admin",
      "weight": 50
    },
    "entityIds": [
      10100,
      100010
    ],
    "hasProperty": true
  },
  "value": {
    "owner": "admin",
    "weight": 100
  }
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-set-issue-property-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|propertyKey|path|string|true|The key of the property. The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|body|body|[BulkIssuePropertyUpdateRequest](#schemabulkissuepropertyupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» expression|body|string|false|EXPERIMENTAL. The Jira expression to calculate the value of the property. The value of the expression must be an object that can be converted to JSON, such as a number, boolean, string, list, or map. The context variables available to the expression are `issue` and `user`. Issues for which the expression returns a value whose JSON representation is longer than 32768 characters are ignored.|
|» filter|body|object|false|The bulk operation filter.|
|» » currentValue|body|object|false|The value of properties to perform the bulk operation on.|
|» » entityIds|body|[integer(int64)]|false|List of issues to perform the bulk operation on.|
|» » hasProperty|body|boolean|false|Whether the bulk operation occurs only when the property is present on or absent from an issue.|
|» value|body|object|false|The value of the property. The value must be a [valid](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4627), non-empty JSON blob. The maximum length is 32768 characters.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errorMessages": [
    "string"
  ],
  "errors": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "status": 0
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errorMessages": [
    "string"
  ],
  "errors": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "status": 0
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-set-issue-property-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|303|See Other|Returned if the request is successful.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|[ErrorCollection](#schemaerrorcollection)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|[ErrorCollection](#schemaerrorcollection)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: write:jira-work )
</aside>

## Bulk delete issue property

<a id="opIdbulkDeleteIssueProperty"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issue/properties/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "currentValue": "deprecated value",
    "entityIds": [
      10100,
      100010
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /rest/api/3/issue/properties/{propertyKey}`

Deletes a property value from multiple issues. The issues to be updated can be specified by filter criteria.

The criteria the filter used to identify eligible issues are:

 *  `entityIds` Only issues from this list are eligible.
 *  `currentValue` Only issues with the property set to this value are eligible.

If both criteria is specified, they are joined with the logical *AND*: only issues that satisfy both criteria are considered eligible.

If no filter criteria are specified, all the issues visible to the user and where the user has the EDIT\_ISSUES permission for the issue are considered eligible.

This operation is:

 *  transactional, either the property is deleted from all eligible issues or, when errors occur, no properties are deleted.
 *  [asynchronous](#async). Follow the `location` link in the response to determine the status of the task and use [Get task](#api-rest-api-3-task-taskId-get) to obtain subsequent updates.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [ project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for each project containing issues.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
 *  *Edit issues* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for each issue.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "currentValue": "deprecated value",
  "entityIds": [
    10100,
    100010
  ]
}
```

```json
  ],

    "property2": "string"
  },
  "status": 0
}
```

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-remote-links">Issue remote links</h1>

This resource represents remote issue links, a way of linking Jira to information in other systems. Use it to get, create, update, and delete remote issue links either by ID or global ID. The global ID provides a way of accessing remote issue links using information about the item's remote system host and remote system identifier.

## Get remote issue links

<a id="opIdgetRemoteIssueLinks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issue/10000/remotelink \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/remotelink`

Returns the remote issue links for an issue. When a remote issue link global ID is provided the record with that global ID is returned, otherwise all remote issue links are returned. Where a global ID includes reserved URL characters these must be escaped in the request. For example, pass `system=http://www.mycompany.com/support&id=1` as `system%3Dhttp%3A%2F%2Fwww.mycompany.com%2Fsupport%26id%3D1`.

This operation requires [issue linking to be active](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yoXKM).

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

<h3 id="get-remote-issue-links-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key of the issue.|
|globalId|query|string|false|The global ID of the remote issue link.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response


## Create or update remote issue link

<a id="opIdcreateOrUpdateRemoteIssueLink"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issue/string/remotelink \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "application": {
      "name": "My Acme Tracker",
      "type": "com.acme.tracker"
    },
    "globalId": "system=http://www.mycompany.com/support&id=1",
    "object": {
      "icon": {
        "title": "Support Ticket",
        "url16x16": "http://www.mycompany.com/support/ticket.png"
      },
      "status": {
        "icon": {
          "link": "http://www.mycompany.com/support?id=1&details=closed",
          "title": "Case Closed",
          "url16x16": "http://www.mycompany.com/support/resolved.png"
        },
        "resolved": true
      },
      "summary": "Customer support issue",
      "title": "TSTSUP-111",
      "url": "http://www.mycompany.com/support?id=1"
    },
    "relationship": "causes"
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/remotelink`

Creates or updates a remote issue link for an issue.

If a `globalId` is provided and a remote issue link with that global ID is found it is updated. Any fields without values in the request are set to null. Otherwise, the remote issue link is created.

This operation requires [issue linking to be active](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yoXKM).

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* and *Link issues* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "application": {
    "name": "My Acme Tracker",
    "type": "com.acme.tracker"
  },
  "globalId": "system=http://www.mycompany.com/support&id=1",
  "object": {
    "icon": {
      "title": "Support Ticket",
      "url16x16": "http://www.mycompany.com/support/ticket.png"
    },
    "status": {
      "icon": {
        "link": "http://www.mycompany.com/support?id=1&details=closed",
        "title": "Case Closed",
        "url16x16": "http://www.mycompany.com/support/resolved.png"
      },
      "resolved": true
    },
    "summary": "Customer support issue",
    "title": "TSTSUP-111",
    "url": "http://www.mycompany.com/support?id=1"
  },
  "relationship": "causes"
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-remote-issue-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key of the issue.|
|body|body|[RemoteIssueLinkRequest](#schemaremoteissuelinkrequest)|true|none|
|» application|body|object|false|Details of the remote application the linked item is in. For example, trello.|
|» » name|body|string|false|The name of the application. Used in conjunction with the (remote) object icon title to display a tooltip for the link's icon. The tooltip takes the format "\[application name\] icon title". Blank items are excluded from the tooltip title. If both items are blank, the icon tooltop displays as "Web Link". Grouping and sorting of links may place links without an application name last.|
|» » type|body|string|false|The name-spaced type of the application, used by registered rendering apps.|
|» globalId|body|string|false|An identifier for the remote item in the remote system. For example, the global ID for a remote item in Confluence would consist of the app ID and page ID, like this: `appId=456&pageId=123`.<br><br>Setting this field enables the remote issue link details to be updated or deleted using remote system and item details as the record identifier, rather than using the record's Jira ID.<br><br>The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|» object|body|object|true|Details of the item linked to.|
|» » icon|body|object|false|Details of the icon for the item. If no icon is defined, the default link icon is used in Jira.|
|» » » link|body|string|false|The URL of the tooltip, used only for a status icon. If not set, the status icon in Jira is not clickable.|
|» » » title|body|string|false|The title of the icon. This is used as follows:<br><br> *  For a status icon it is used as a tooltip on the icon. If not set, the status icon doesn't display a tooltip in Jira.<br> *  For the remote object icon it is used in conjunction with the application name to display a tooltip for the link's icon. The tooltip takes the format "\[application name\] icon title". Blank itemsare excluded from the tooltip title. If both items are blank, the icon tooltop displays as "Web Link".|
|» » » url16x16|body|string|false|The URL of an icon that displays at 16x16 pixel in Jira.|
|» » status|body|object|false|The status of the item.|
|» » » icon|body|object|false|Details of the icon representing the status. If not provided, no status icon displays in Jira.|
|» » » » link|body|string|false|The URL of the tooltip, used only for a status icon. If not set, the status icon in Jira is not clickable.|
|» » » » title|body|string|false|The title of the icon. This is used as follows:<br><br> *  For a status icon it is used as a tooltip on the icon. If not set, the status icon doesn't display a tooltip in Jira.<br> *  For the remote object icon it is used in conjunction with the application name to display a tooltip for the link's icon. The tooltip takes the format "\[application name\] icon title". Blank itemsare excluded from the tooltip title. If both items are blank, the icon tooltop displays as "Web Link".|
|» » » » url16x16|body|string|false|The URL of an icon that displays at 16x16 pixel in Jira.|
|» » » resolved|body|boolean|false|Whether the item is resolved. If set to "true", the link to the issue is displayed in a strikethrough font, otherwise the link displays in normal font.|
|» » summary|body|string|false|The summary details of the item.|
|» » title|body|string|true|The title of the item.|
|» » url|body|string|true|The URL of the item.|
|» relationship|body|string|false|Description of the relationship between the issue and the linked item. If not set, the relationship description "links to" is used in Jira.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"id\":10000,\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/issue/MKY-1/remotelink/10000\"}"
```

> 201 Response

```json

```

> 400 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[],\"errors\":{\"title\":\"'title' is required.\"}}"
```

|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|

## Delete remote issue link by global ID

<a id="opIddeleteRemoteIssueLinkByGlobalId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/rest/api/3/issue/10000/remotelink?globalId=system%3Dhttp%3A%2F%2Fwww.mycompany.com%2Fsupport%26id%3D1' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/remotelink`

Deletes the remote issue link from the issue using the link's global ID. Where the global ID includes reserved URL characters these must be escaped in the request. For example, pass `system=http://www.mycompany.com/support&id=1` as `system%3Dhttp%3A%2F%2Fwww.mycompany.com%2Fsupport%26id%3D1`.

This operation requires [issue linking to be active](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yoXKM).

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* and *Link issues* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is implemented, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

<h3 id="delete-remote-issue-link-by-global-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key of the issue.|
|globalId|query|string|true|The global ID of a remote issue link.|

<h3 id="delete-remote-issue-link-by-global-id-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the request is successful.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if a global ID isn't provided.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to link issues.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the issue or remote issue link is not found or the user does not have permission to view the issue.|None|

Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: write:jira-work )

## Create resolution

<a id="opIdcreateResolution"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/resolution \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "My resolution description",
    "name": "My new resolution"
```

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-search">Issue search</h1>

This resource represents various ways to search for issues. Use it to search for issues with a JQL query and find issues to populate an issue picker.

## Get issue picker suggestions

<a id="opIdgetIssuePickerResource"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issue/picker \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issue/picker`

Returns lists of issues matching a query string. Use this resource to provide auto-completion suggestions when the user is looking for an issue using a word or string.

This operation returns two lists:

 *  `History Search` which includes issues from the user's history of created, edited, or viewed issues that contain the string in the `query` parameter.
 *  `Current Search` which includes issues that match the JQL expression in `currentJQL` and contain the string in the `query` parameter.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** None.

<h3 id="get-issue-picker-suggestions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|false|A string to match against text fields in the issue such as title, description, or comments.|
|currentJQL|query|string|false|A JQL query defining a list of issues to search for the query term. Note that `username` and `userkey` cannot be used as search terms for this parameter, due to privacy reasons. Use `accountId` instead.|
|currentIssueKey|query|string|false|The key of an issue to exclude from search results. For example, the issue the user is viewing when they perform this query.|
|currentProjectId|query|string|false|The ID of a project that suggested issues must belong to.|
|showSubTasks|query|boolean|false|Indicate whether to include subtasks in the suggestions list.|
|showSubTaskParent|query|boolean|false|When `currentIssueKey` is a subtask, whether to include the parent issue in the suggestions if it matches the query.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "sections": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "issues": [
        {
          "id": 0,
          "img": "string",
          "key": "string",
          "keyHtml": "string",
          "summary": "string",
          "summaryText": "string"
        }
      ],
      "label": "string",
      "msg": "string",
      "sub": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-issue-picker-suggestions-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[IssuePickerSuggestions](#schemaissuepickersuggestions)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Check issues against JQL

<a id="opIdmatchIssues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/jql/match \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "issueIds": [
      10001,
      1000,
      10042
    ],
    "jqls": [
      "project = FOO",
      "issuetype = Bug",
      "summary ~ \"some text\" AND project in (FOO, BAR)"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/jql/match`

Checks whether one or more issues would be returned by one or more JQL queries.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** None, however, issues are only matched against JQL queries where the user has:

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "issueIds": [
    10001,
    1000,
    10042
  ],
  "jqls": [
    "project = FOO",
    "issuetype = Bug",
    "summary ~ \"some text\" AND project in (FOO, BAR)"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="check-issues-against-jql-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IssuesAndJQLQueries](#schemaissuesandjqlqueries)|true|none|
|» issueIds|body|[integer(int64)]|true|A list of issue IDs.|
|» jqls|body|[string]|true|A list of JQL queries.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"matches\":[{\"matchedIssues\":[10000,10004],\"errors\":[]},{\"matchedIssues\":[100134,10025,10236],\"errors\":[]},{\"matchedIssues\":[],\"errors\":[]},{\"matchedIssues\":[],\"errors\":[\"Invalid JQL: broken = value\"]}]}"
```

<h3 id="check-issues-against-jql-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[IssueMatches](#schemaissuematches)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if `jqls` exceeds the maximum number of JQL queries or `issueIds` exceeds the maximum number of issue IDs.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Search for issues using JQL (GET)

<a id="opIdsearchForIssuesUsingJql"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/search \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/search`

Searches for issues using [JQL](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/egORLQ).

If the JQL query expression is too large to be encoded as a query parameter, use the [POST](#api-rest-api-3-search-post) version of this resource.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Issues are included in the response where the user has:

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project containing the issue.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

<h3 id="search-for-issues-using-jql-get-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|jql|query|string|false|The [JQL](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/egORLQ) that defines the search. Note:<br><br> *  If no JQL expression is provided, all issues are returned.<br> *  `username` and `userkey` cannot be used as search terms due to privacy reasons. Use `accountId` instead.<br> *  If a user has hidden their email address in their user profile, partial matches of the email address will not find the user. An exact match is required.|
|startAt|query|integer(int32)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page. To manage page size, Jira may return fewer items per page where a large number of fields are requested. The greatest number of items returned per page is achieved when requesting `id` or `key` only.|
|validateQuery|query|string|false|Determines how to validate the JQL query and treat the validation results. Supported values are:<br><br> *  `strict` Returns a 400 response code if any errors are found, along with a list of all errors (and warnings).<br> *  `warn` Returns all errors as warnings.<br> *  `none` No validation is performed.<br> *  `true` *Deprecated* A legacy synonym for `strict`.<br> *  `false` *Deprecated* A legacy synonym for `warn`.<br><br>Note: If the JQL is not correctly formed a 400 response code is returned, regardless of the `validateQuery` value.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A list of fields to return for each issue, use it to retrieve a subset of fields. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `*all` Returns all fields.<br> *  `*navigable` Returns navigable fields.<br> *  Any issue field, prefixed with a minus to exclude.<br><br>Examples:<br><br> *  `summary,comment` Returns only the summary and comments fields.<br> *  `-description` Returns all navigable (default) fields except description.<br> *  `*all,-comment` Returns all fields except comments.<br><br>This parameter may be specified multiple times. For example, `fields=field1,field2&fields=field3`.<br><br>Note: All navigable fields are returned by default. This differs from [GET issue](#api-rest-api-3-issue-issueIdOrKey-get) where the default is all fields.|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information about issues in the response. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `renderedFields` Returns field values rendered in HTML format.<br> *  `names` Returns the display name of each field.<br> *  `schema` Returns the schema describing a field type.<br> *  `transitions` Returns all possible transitions for the issue.<br> *  `operations` Returns all possible operations for the issue.<br> *  `editmeta` Returns information about how each field can be edited.<br> *  `changelog` Returns a list of recent updates to an issue, sorted by date, starting from the most recent.<br> *  `versionedRepresentations` Instead of `fields`, returns `versionedRepresentations` a JSON array containing each version of a field's value, with the highest numbered item representing the most recent version.|
|properties|query|[string]|false|A list of issue property keys for issue properties to include in the results. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Multiple properties can also be provided using an ampersand separated list. For example, `properties=prop1,prop2&properties=prop3`. A maximum of 5 issue property keys can be specified.|
|fieldsByKeys|query|boolean|false|Reference fields by their key (rather than ID).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|validateQuery|strict|
|validateQuery|warn|
|validateQuery|none|
|validateQuery|true|
|validateQuery|false|

> Example responses

## Search for issues using JQL (POST)

<a id="opIdsearchForIssuesUsingJqlPost"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "expand": [
      "names",
      "schema",
      "operations"
    ],
    "fields": [
      "summary",
      "status",
      "assignee"
    ],
    "fieldsByKeys": false,
    "jql": "project = HSP",
    "maxResults": 15,
    "startAt": 0
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/search`

Searches for issues using [JQL](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/egORLQ).

There is a [GET](#api-rest-api-3-search-get) version of this resource that can be used for smaller JQL query expressions.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Issues are included in the response where the user has:

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project containing the issue.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expand": [
    "names",
    "schema",
    "operations"
  ],
  "fields": [
    "summary",
    "status",
    "assignee"
  ],
  "fieldsByKeys": false,
  "jql": "project = HSP",
  "maxResults": 15,
  "startAt": 0
}
```

<h3 id="search-for-issues-using-jql-post-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SearchRequestBean](#schemasearchrequestbean)|true|A JSON object containing the search request.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Use [expand](em>#expansion) to include additional information about issues in the response. Note that, unlike the majority of instances where `expand` is specified, `expand` is defined as a list of values. The expand options are:<br><br> *  `renderedFields` Returns field values rendered in HTML format.<br> *  `names` Returns the display name of each field.<br> *  `schema` Returns the schema describing a field type.<br> *  `transitions` Returns all possible transitions for the issue.<br> *  `operations` Returns all possible operations for the issue.<br> *  `editmeta` Returns information about how each field can be edited.<br> *  `changelog` Returns a list of recent updates to an issue, sorted by date, starting from the most recent.<br> *  `versionedRepresentations` Instead of `fields`, returns `versionedRepresentations` a JSON array containing each version of a field's value, with the highest numbered item representing the most recent version.|
|» fields|body|[string]|false|A list of fields to return for each issue, use it to retrieve a subset of fields. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `*all` Returns all fields.<br> *  `*navigable` Returns navigable fields.<br> *  Any issue field, prefixed with a minus to exclude.<br><br>The default is `*navigable`.<br><br>Examples:<br><br> *  `summary,comment` Returns the summary and comments fields only.<br> *  `-description` Returns all navigable (default) fields except description.<br> *  `*all,-comment` Returns all fields except comments.<br><br>Multiple `fields` parameters can be included in a request.<br><br>Note: All navigable fields are returned by default. This differs from [GET issue](#api-rest-api-3-issue-issueIdOrKey-get) where the default is all fields.|
|» fieldsByKeys|body|boolean|false|Reference fields by their key (rather than ID). The default is `false`.|
|» jql|body|string|false|A [JQL](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/egORLQ) expression.|
|» maxResults|body|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|» properties|body|[string]|false|A list of up to 5 issue properties to include in the results. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list.|
|» startAt|body|integer(int32)|false|The index of the first item to return in the page of results (page offset). The base index is `0`.|
|» validateQuery|body|string|false|Determines how to validate the JQL query and treat the validation results. Supported values:<br><br> *  `strict` Returns a 400 response code if any errors are found, along with a list of all errors (and warnings).<br> *  `warn` Returns all errors as warnings.<br> *  `none` No validation is performed.<br> *  `true` *Deprecated* A legacy synonym for `strict`.<br> *  `false` *Deprecated* A legacy synonym for `warn`.<br><br>The default is `strict`.<br><br>Note: If the JQL is not correctly formed a 400 response code is returned, regardless of the `validateQuery` value.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» validateQuery|strict|
|» validateQuery|warn|
|» validateQuery|none|
|» validateQuery|true|
|» validateQuery|false|

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-security-level">Issue security level</h1>

This resource represents issue security levels. Use it to obtain the details of any issue security level. For more information about issue security levels, see [Configuring issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg).

## Get issue security level members

<a id="opIdgetIssueSecurityLevelMembers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issuesecurityschemes/0/members \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issuesecurityschemes/{issueSecuritySchemeId}/members`

Returns issue security level members.

Only issue security level members in context of classic projects are returned.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="get-issue-security-level-members-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueSecuritySchemeId|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the issue security scheme. Use the [Get issue security schemes](#api-rest-api-3-issuesecurityschemes-get) operation to get a list of issue security scheme IDs.|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|issueSecurityLevelId|query|[integer(int64)]|false|The list of issue security level IDs. To include multiple issue security levels separate IDs with ampersand: `issueSecurityLevelId=10000&issueSecurityLevelId=10001`.|
|expand|query|string|false|Use expand to include additional information in the response. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `all` Returns all expandable information.<br> *  `field` Returns information about the custom field granted the permission.<br> *  `group` Returns information about the group that is granted the permission.<br> *  `projectRole` Returns information about the project role granted the permission.<br> *  `user` Returns information about the user who is granted the permission.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"maxResults\":100,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":3,\"isLast\":true,\"values\":[{\"id\":10000,\"issueSecurityLevelId\":10020,\"holder\":{\"type\":\"user\",\"user\":{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/user?accountId=5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"emailAddress\":\"mia@example.com\",\"avatarUrls\":{\"48x48\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=48&s=48\",\"24x24\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=24&s=24\",\"16x16\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=16&s=16\",\"32x32\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=32&s=32\"},\"displayName\":\"Mia Krystof\",\"active\":true,\"timeZone\":\"Australia/Sydney\"},\"expand\":\"user\"}},{\"id\":10001,\"issueSecurityLevelId\":10020,\"holder\":{\"type\":\"group\",\"parameter\":\"jira-core-users\",\"value\":\"9c559b11-6c5d-4f96-992c-a746cabab28b\",\"expand\":\"group\"}},{\"id\":10002,\"issueSecurityLevelId\":10021,\"holder\":{\"type\":\"assignee\"}}]}"
```

<h3 id="get-issue-security-level-members-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PageBeanIssueSecurityLevelMember](#schemapagebeanissuesecuritylevelmember)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is not valid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if no issue security level members are found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

## Get issue security level

<a id="opIdgetIssueSecurityLevel"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/securitylevel/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/securitylevel/{id}`

Returns details of an issue security level.

Use [Get issue security scheme](#api-rest-api-3-issuesecurityschemes-id-get) to obtain the IDs of issue security levels associated with the issue security scheme.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** None.

<h3 id="get-issue-security-level-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the issue security level.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/securitylevel/10021\",\"id\":\"10021\",\"description\":\"Only the reporter and internal staff can see this issue.\",\"name\":\"Reporter Only\"}"
```

<h3 id="get-issue-security-level-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[SecurityLevel](#schemasecuritylevel)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the issue security level is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-security-schemes">Issue security schemes</h1>

This resource represents issue security schemes. Use it to get an issue security scheme or list of issues security schemes.

Issue security schemes control which users or groups of users can view an issue. When an issue security scheme is associated with a project, its security levels can be applied to issues in that project. Sub-tasks also inherit the security level of their parent issue.

## Get issue security schemes

<a id="opIdgetIssueSecuritySchemes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issuesecurityschemes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issuesecurityschemes`

Returns all [issue security schemes](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg).

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"issueSecuritySchemes\":[{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuesecurityschemes/10000\",\"id\":10000,\"name\":\"Default Issue Security Scheme\",\"description\":\"Description for the default issue security scheme\",\"defaultSecurityLevelId\":10021}]}"
```

<h3 id="get-issue-security-schemes-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[SecuritySchemes](#schemasecurityschemes)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to administer issue security schemes.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-project )
</aside>

## Get issue security scheme

Returns an issue security scheme along with its security levels.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

```json
"{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuesecurityschemes/10000\",\"id\":10000,\"name\":\"Default Issue Security Scheme\",\"description\":\"Description for the default issue security scheme\",\"defaultSecurityLevelId\":10021,\"levels\":[{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/securitylevel/10021\",\"id\":\"10021\",\"description\":\"Only the reporter and internal staff can see this issue.\",\"name\":\"Reporter Only\"}]}"
```

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-project )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-types">Issue types</h1>

This resource represents issues types. Use it to:

 *  get, create, update, and delete issue types.
 *  get all issue types for a user.
 *  get alternative issue types.
 *  set an avatar for an issue type.

## Get all issue types for user

<a id="opIdgetIssueAllTypes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issuetype \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issuetype`

Returns all issue types.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Issue types are only returned as follows:

 *  if the user has the *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg), all issue types are returned.
 *  if the user has the *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for one or more projects, the issue types associated with the projects the user has permission to browse are returned.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"[{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issueType/3\",\"id\":\"3\",\"description\":\"A task that needs to be done.\",\"iconUrl\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/secure/viewavatar?size=xsmall&avatarId=10299&avatarType=issuetype\\\",\",\"name\":\"Task\",\"subtask\":false,\"avatarId\":1,\"hierarchyLevel\":0},{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issueType/1\",\"id\":\"1\",\"description\":\"A problem with the software.\",\"iconUrl\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/secure/viewavatar?size=xsmall&avatarId=10316&avatarType=issuetype\\\",\",\"name\":\"Bug\",\"subtask\":false,\"avatarId\":10002,\"entityId\":\"9d7dd6f7-e8b6-4247-954b-7b2c9b2a5ba2\",\"hierarchyLevel\":0,\"scope\":{\"type\":\"PROJECT\",\"project\":{\"id\":\"10000\",\"key\":\"KEY\",\"name\":\"Next Gen Project\"}}}]"
```

<h3 id="get-all-issue-types-for-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|

<h3 id="get-all-issue-types-for-user-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[IssueTypeDetails](#schemaissuetypedetails)]|false|none|none|

## Create issue type

<a id="opIdcreateIssueType"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issuetype \

  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "description",
    "name": "name",
    "type": "standard"
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/issuetype`

Creates an issue type and adds it to the default issue type scheme.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "description",
  "name": "name",
  "type": "standard"
}
```

<h3 id="create-issue-type-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IssueTypeCreateBean](#schemaissuetypecreatebean)|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the issue type.|
|» hierarchyLevel|body|integer(int32)|false|The hierarchy level of the issue type. Use:<br><br> *  `-1` for Subtask.<br> *  `0` for Base.<br><br>Defaults to `0`.|
|» name|body|string|true|The unique name for the issue type. The maximum length is 60 characters.|
|» type|body|string|false|Deprecated. Use `hierarchyLevel` instead. See the [deprecation notice](https://community.developer.atlassian.com/t/deprecation-of-the-epic-link-parent-link-and-other-related-fields-in-rest-apis-and-webhooks/54048) for details.<br><br>Whether the issue type is `subtype` or `standard`. Defaults to `standard`.|

## Load issue type avatar

<a id="opIdcreateIssueTypeAvatar"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/rest/api/3/issuetype/string/avatar2?size=0' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: */*' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /rest/api/3/issuetype/{id}/avatar2`

Loads an avatar for the issue type.

Specify the avatar's local file location in the body of the request. Also, include the following headers:

 *  `X-Atlassian-Token: no-check` To prevent XSRF protection blocking the request, for more information see [Special Headers](#special-request-headers).
 *  `Content-Type: image/image type` Valid image types are JPEG, GIF, or PNG.

For example:  
`curl --request POST \ --user email@example.com:<api_token> \ --header 'X-Atlassian-Token: no-check' \ --header 'Content-Type: image/< image_type>' \ --data-binary "<@/path/to/file/with/your/avatar>" \ --url 'https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuetype/{issueTypeId}'This`

The avatar is cropped to a square. If no crop parameters are specified, the square originates at the top left of the image. The length of the square's sides is set to the smaller of the height or width of the image.

The cropped image is then used to create avatars of 16x16, 24x24, 32x32, and 48x48 in size.

After creating the avatar, use [ Update issue type](#api-rest-api-3-issuetype-id-put) to set it as the issue type's displayed avatar.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="load-issue-type-avatar-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the issue type.|
|x|query|integer(int32)|false|The X coordinate of the top-left corner of the crop region.|
|y|query|integer(int32)|false|The Y coordinate of the top-left corner of the crop region.|
|size|query|integer(int32)|true|The length of each side of the crop region.|
|body|body|object|true|none|

> Example responses

> 201 Response


<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-type-schemes">Issue type schemes</h1>

This resource represents issue type schemes in classic projects. Use it to:

 *  get issue type schemes and a list of the projects that use them.
 *  associate issue type schemes with projects.
 *  add issue types to issue type schemes.
 *  delete issue types from issue type schemes.
 *  create, update, and delete issue type schemes.
 *  change the order of issue types in issue type schemes.

## Get all issue type schemes

<a id="opIdgetAllIssueTypeSchemes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issuetypescheme \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issuetypescheme`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of issue type schemes.

Only issue type schemes used in classic projects are returned.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="get-all-issue-type-schemes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|id|query|[integer(int64)]|false|The list of issue type schemes IDs. To include multiple IDs, provide an ampersand-separated list. For example, `id=10000&id=10001`.|
|orderBy|query|string|false|[Order](#ordering) the results by a field:<br><br> *  `name` Sorts by issue type scheme name.<br> *  `id` Sorts by issue type scheme ID.|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information in the response. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `projects` For each issue type schemes, returns information about the projects the issue type scheme is assigned to.<br> *  `issueTypes` For each issue type schemes, returns information about the issueTypes the issue type scheme have.|
|queryString|query|string|false|String used to perform a case-insensitive partial match with issue type scheme name.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|orderBy|name|
|orderBy|-name|
|orderBy|+name|
|orderBy|id|
|orderBy|-id|
|orderBy|+id|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"maxResults\":100,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":3,\"isLast\":true,\"values\":[{\"id\":\"10000\",\"name\":\"Default Issue Type Scheme\",\"description\":\"Default issue type scheme is the list of global issue types. All newly created issue types will automatically be added to this scheme.\",\"defaultIssueTypeId\":\"10003\",\"isDefault\":true},{\"id\":\"10001\",\"name\":\"SUP: Kanban Issue Type Scheme\",\"description\":\"A collection of issue types suited to use in a kanban style project.\",\"projects\":{\"maxResults\":100,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":1,\"isLast\":true,\"values\":[{\"self\":\"project/EX\",\"id\":\"10000\",\"key\":\"EX\",\"name\":\"Example\",\"projectTypeKey\":\"ProjectTypeKey{key='software'}\",\"simplified\":false,\"avatarUrls\":{\"48x48\":\"secure/projectavatar?size=large&pid=10000\",\"24x24\":\"secure/projectavatar?size=small&pid=10000\",\"16x16\":\"secure/projectavatar?size=xsmall&pid=10000\",\"32x32\":\"secure/projectavatar?size=medium&pid=10000\"},\"projectCategory\":{\"id\":\"10000\",\"description\":\"Project category description\",\"name\":\"A project category\"}}]}},{\"id\":\"10002\",\"name\":\"HR: Scrum issue type scheme\",\"description\":\"\",\"defaultIssueTypeId\":\"10004\",\"issueTypes\":{\"maxResults\":100,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":1,\"isLast\":true,\"values\":[{\"id\":\"1000L\",\"description\":\"Improvement Issue Type\",\"iconUrl\":\"www.example.com\",\"name\":\"Improvements\",\"subtask\":true,\"hierarchyLevel\":-1}]}}]}"
```

## Create issue type scheme

<a id="opIdcreateIssueTypeScheme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issuetypescheme \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "defaultIssueTypeId": "10002",
    "description": "A collection of issue types suited to use in a kanban style project.",
    "issueTypeIds": [
      "10001",
      "10002",
      "10003"
    ],
    "name": "Kanban Issue Type Scheme"
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/issuetypescheme`

Creates an issue type scheme.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "defaultIssueTypeId": "10002",
  "description": "A collection of issue types suited to use in a kanban style project.",
  "issueTypeIds": [
    "10001",
    "10002",
    "10003"
  ],
  "name": "Kanban Issue Type Scheme"
}
```

<h3 id="create-issue-type-scheme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IssueTypeSchemeDetails](#schemaissuetypeschemedetails)|true|none|
|» defaultIssueTypeId|body|string|false|The ID of the default issue type of the issue type scheme. This ID must be included in `issueTypeIds`.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the issue type scheme. The maximum length is 4000 characters.|
|» issueTypeIds|body|[string]|true|The list of issue types IDs of the issue type scheme. At least one standard issue type ID is required.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the issue type scheme. The name must be unique. The maximum length is 255 characters.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
"{\"issueTypeSchemeId\":\"10010\"}"
```

> 400 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"The default issue type ID has to be present in issue type IDs list.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 403 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"Only Jira administrators can access issue type schemes.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 409 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"The name is used by another scheme.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

<h3 id="create-issue-type-scheme-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|201|Created|Returned if the request is successful.|[IssueTypeSchemeID](#schemaissuetypeschemeid)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is not valid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the required permissions.|None|
|409|Conflict|Returned if the scheme name is used by another scheme.|None|

basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )

## Assign issue type scheme to project

<a id="opIdassignIssueTypeSchemeToProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issuetypescheme/project \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \

    "issueTypeSchemeId": "10000",
    "projectId": "10000"
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/issuetypescheme/project`

Assigns an issue type scheme to a project.

If any issues in the project are assigned issue types not present in the new scheme, the operation will fail. To complete the assignment those issues must be updated to use issue types in the new scheme.

Issue type schemes can only be assigned to classic projects.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "issueTypeSchemeId": "10000",
  "projectId": "10000"
}
```

<h3 id="assign-issue-type-scheme-to-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|body|body|[IssueTypeSchemeProjectAssociation](#schemaissuetypeschemeprojectassociation)|true|none|
|» issueTypeSchemeId|body|string|true|The ID of the issue type scheme.|
|» projectId|body|string|true|The ID of the project.|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
null
```

> 400 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"This issue type scheme can't be assigned to the project. This is because some issues in this project use issue types not present in the scheme. Before assigning the scheme to the project, update the issue types on these issues: 7\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"Only Jira administrators can access issue type schemes.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"The issue type scheme was not found.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

## Change order of issue types

<a id="opIdreorderIssueTypesInIssueTypeScheme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issuetypescheme/0/issuetype/move \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "after": "10008",
    "issueTypeIds": [
      "10001",
      "10004",
      "10002"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/issuetypescheme/{issueTypeSchemeId}/issuetype/move`

Changes the order of issue types in an issue type scheme.

The request body parameters must meet the following requirements:

 *  all of the issue types must belong to the issue type scheme.
 *  either `after` or `position` must be provided.
 *  the issue type in `after` must not be in the issue type list.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "after": "10008",
  "issueTypeIds": [
    "10001",
    "10004",
    "10002"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="change-order-of-issue-types-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueTypeSchemeId|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the issue type scheme.|
|body|body|[OrderOfIssueTypes](#schemaorderofissuetypes)|true|none|
|» after|body|string|false|The ID of the issue type to place the moved issue types after. Required if `position` isn't provided.|
|» issueTypeIds|body|[string]|true|A list of the issue type IDs to move. The order of the issue type IDs in the list is the order they are given after the move.|

|» position|Last|

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-type-screen-schemes">Issue type screen schemes</h1>

This resource represents issue type screen schemes. Use it to:

 *  get issue type screen schemes and a list of the projects that use them.
 *  create issue type screen schemes.
 *  update issue type screen schemes.
 *  delete issue type screen schemes.
 *  associate issue type screen schemes with projects.
 *  append issue type to screen scheme mappings to issue type screen schemes.
 *  remove issue type to screen scheme mappings from issue type screen schemes.
 *  update default screen scheme of issue type screen scheme.

## Get issue type screen schemes

<a id="opIdgetIssueTypeScreenSchemes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issuetypescreenscheme \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issuetypescreenscheme`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of issue type screen schemes.

Only issue type screen schemes used in classic projects are returned.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="get-issue-type-screen-schemes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|id|query|[integer(int64)]|false|The list of issue type screen scheme IDs. To include multiple IDs, provide an ampersand-separated list. For example, `id=10000&id=10001`.|
|queryString|query|string|false|String used to perform a case-insensitive partial match with issue type screen scheme name.|
|orderBy|query|string|false|[Order](#ordering) the results by a field:<br><br> *  `name` Sorts by issue type screen scheme name.<br> *  `id` Sorts by issue type screen scheme ID.|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information in the response. This parameter accepts `projects` that, for each issue type screen schemes, returns information about the projects the issue type screen scheme is assigned to.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|orderBy|name|
|orderBy|-name|
|orderBy|+name|
|orderBy|id|
|orderBy|-id|
|orderBy|+id|

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"maxResults\":100,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":2,\"isLast\":true,\"values\":[{\"id\":\"1\",\"name\":\"Default Issue Type Screen Scheme\",\"description\":\"The default issue type screen scheme\"},{\"id\":\"10000\",\"name\":\"Office issue type screen scheme\",\"description\":\"Managing office projects\",\"projects\":{\"maxResults\":100,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":1,\"isLast\":true,\"values\":[{\"self\":\"project/EX\",\"id\":\"10000\",\"key\":\"EX\",\"name\":\"Example\",\"projectTypeKey\":\"ProjectTypeKey{key='software'}\",\"simplified\":false,\"avatarUrls\":{\"48x48\":\"secure/projectavatar?size=large&pid=10000\",\"24x24\":\"secure/projectavatar?size=small&pid=10000\",\"16x16\":\"secure/projectavatar?size=xsmall&pid=10000\",\"32x32\":\"secure/projectavatar?size=medium&pid=10000\"},\"projectCategory\":{\"id\":\"10000\",\"description\":\"Project category description\",\"name\":\"A project category\"}}]}}]}"
```

## Create issue type screen scheme

<a id="opIdcreateIssueTypeScreenScheme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issuetypescreenscheme \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "issueTypeMappings": [
      {
        "issueTypeId": "default",
        "screenSchemeId": "10001"
      },
      {
        "issueTypeId": "10001",
        "screenSchemeId": "10002"
      },
      {
        "issueTypeId": "10002",
        "screenSchemeId": "10002"
      }
    ],
    "name": "Scrum issue type screen scheme"
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/issuetypescreenscheme`

Creates an issue type screen scheme.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "issueTypeMappings": [
    {
      "issueTypeId": "default",
      "screenSchemeId": "10001"
    },
    {
      "issueTypeId": "10001",
      "screenSchemeId": "10002"
    },
    {
      "issueTypeId": "10002",
      "screenSchemeId": "10002"
    }
  ],
  "name": "Scrum issue type screen scheme"
}
```

<h3 id="create-issue-type-screen-scheme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IssueTypeScreenSchemeDetails](#schemaissuetypescreenschemedetails)|true|An issue type screen scheme bean.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the issue type screen scheme. The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|» issueTypeMappings|body|[[IssueTypeScreenSchemeMapping](#schemaissuetypescreenschememapping)]|true|The IDs of the screen schemes for the issue type IDs and *default*. A *default* entry is required to create an issue type screen scheme, it defines the mapping for all issue types without a screen scheme.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the issue type screen scheme. The name must be unique. The maximum length is 255 characters.|


> 400 Response

```json

```


> 409 Response


|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|

|404|Not Found|Returned if the issue type or screen scheme is not found.|None|

```bash
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/issuetypescreenscheme/{issueTypeScreenSchemeId}/mapping/default`

Updates the default screen scheme of an issue type screen scheme. The default screen scheme is used for all unmapped issue types.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

```json
{
  "screenSchemeId": "10010"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|

|body|body|[UpdateDefaultScreenScheme](#schemaupdatedefaultscreenscheme)|true|none|
|» screenSchemeId|body|string|true|The ID of the screen scheme.|

```json
null
```



> 404 Response


|---|---|---|---|

|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is not valid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the required permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the issue type screen scheme or the screen screen is not found, or the screen scheme isn't used in classic projects.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-type-properties">Issue type properties</h1>

This resource represents [issue type](#api-group-Issue-types) properties, which provides for storing custom data against an issue type. Use it to get, create, and delete issue type properties as well as obtain the keys of all properties on a issues type. Issue type properties are a type of [entity property](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/jira-entity-properties/).

## Get issue type property keys

<a id="opIdgetIssueTypePropertyKeys"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issuetype/string/properties \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issuetype/{issueTypeId}/properties`

Returns all the [issue type property](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/storing-data-without-a-database/#a-id-jira-entity-properties-a-jira-entity-properties) keys of the issue type.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg) to get the property keys of any issue type.
 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) to get the property keys of any issue types associated with the projects the user has permission to browse.

<h3 id="get-issue-type-property-keys-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueTypeId|path|string|true|The ID of the issue type.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"keys\":[{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/EX-2/properties/issue.support\",\"key\":\"issue.support\"}]}"
```

<h3 id="get-issue-type-property-keys-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PropertyKeys](#schemapropertykeys)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the issue type ID is invalid.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if:<br><br> *  the issue type is not found.<br> *  the user does not have the required permissions.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Get issue type property

<a id="opIdgetIssueTypeProperty"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issuetype/string/properties/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issuetype/{issueTypeId}/properties/{propertyKey}`

Returns the key and value of the [issue type property](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/storing-data-without-a-database/#a-id-jira-entity-properties-a-jira-entity-properties).

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg) to get the details of any issue type.
 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) to get the details of any issue types associated with the projects the user has permission to browse.

<h3 id="get-issue-type-property-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueTypeId|path|string|true|The ID of the issue type.|
|propertyKey|path|string|true|The key of the property. Use [Get issue type property keys](#api-rest-api-3-issuetype-issueTypeId-properties-get) to get a list of all issue type property keys.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"key\":\"issue.support\",\"value\":{\"system.conversation.id\":\"b1bf38be-5e94-4b40-a3b8-9278735ee1e6\",\"system.support.time\":\"1m\"}}"
```

<h3 id="get-issue-type-property-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[EntityProperty](#schemaentityproperty)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the issue type ID is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the issue type or property is not found or the user does not have the required permissions.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Set issue type property

<a id="opIdsetIssueTypeProperty"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issuetype/string/properties/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "number": 5,
    "string": "string-value"
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/issuetype/{issueTypeId}/properties/{propertyKey}`

Creates or updates the value of the [issue type property](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/storing-data-without-a-database/#a-id-jira-entity-properties-a-jira-entity-properties). Use this resource to store and update data against an issue type.

The value of the request body must be a [valid](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4627), non-empty JSON blob. The maximum length is 32768 characters.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "number": 5,
  "string": "string-value"
}
```

<h3 id="set-issue-type-property-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueTypeId|path|string|true|The ID of the issue type.|
|propertyKey|path|string|true|The key of the issue type property. The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|body|body|object|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
null
```

> 201 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="set-issue-type-property-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the issue type property is updated.|Inline|
|201|Created|Returned if the issue type property is created.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if:<br><br> *  the issue type ID is invalid.<br> *  a property value is not provided.<br> *  the property value JSON content is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to modify the issue type.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if:<br><br> *  the issue type is not found.<br> *  the user does not have the permission view the issue type.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-votes">Issue votes</h1>

This resource represents votes cast by users on an issue. Use it to get details of votes on an issue as well as cast and withdrawal votes.

## Get votes

<a id="opIdgetVotes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issue/string/votes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/votes`

Returns details about the votes on an issue.

This operation requires the **Allow users to vote on issues** option to be *ON*. This option is set in General configuration for Jira. See [Configuring Jira application options](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/uYXKM) for details.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is ini
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

Note that users with the necessary permissions for this operation but without the *View voters and watchers* project permissions are not returned details in the `voters` field.

<h3 id="get-votes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key of the issue.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/issue/MKY-1/votes\",\"votes\":24,\"hasVoted\":true,\"voters\":[{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/user?accountId=5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"key\":\"\",\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"accountType\":\"atlassian\",\"name\":\"\",\"avatarUrls\":{\"48x48\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=48&s=48\",\"24x24\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=24&s=24\",\"16x16\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=16&s=16\",\"32x32\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=32&s=32\"},\"displayName\":\"Mia Krystof\",\"active\":false}]}"
```

<h3 id="get-votes-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[Votes](#schemavotes)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if:<br><br> *  voting is disabled.<br> *  the user does not have permission to view the issue.<br> *  the issue is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Add vote

<a id="opIdaddVote"></a>

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issue/string/votes \
```

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key of the issue.|

> Example responses

```json
null
```

|---|---|---|---|

|404|Not Found|Returned if:<br><br> *  voting is disabled.<br> *  the issue is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: write:jira-work )
</aside>

## Delete vote

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issue/string/votes \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/votes`

Deletes a user's vote from an issue. This is the equivalent of the user clicking *Unvote* on an issue in Jira.

This operation requires the **Allow users to vote on issues** option to be *ON*. This option is set in General configuration for Jira. See [Configuring Jira application options](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/uYXKM) for details.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key of the issue.|

<h3 id="delete-vote-responses">Responses</h3>

|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if:<br><br> *  voting is disabled.<br> *  the user has not voted on the issue.<br> *  the issue is not found.|None|

basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: write:jira-work )

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-watchers">Issue watchers</h1>

This resource represents users watching an issue. Use it to get details of users watching an issue as well as start and stop a user watching an issue.

## Get is watching issue bulk

<a id="opIdgetIsWatchingIssueBulk"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issue/watching \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "issueIds": [
      "10001",
      "10002",
      "10005"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/issue/watching`

Returns, for the user, details of the watched status of issues from a list. If an issue ID is invalid, the returned watched status is `false`.

This operation requires the **Allow users to watch issues** option to be *ON*. This option is set in General configuration for Jira. See [Configuring Jira application options](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/uYXKM) for details.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "issueIds": [
    "10001",
    "10002",
    "10005"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-is-watching-issue-bulk-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IssueList](#schemaissuelist)|true|A list of issue IDs.|
|» issueIds|body|[string]|true|The list of issue IDs.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"issuesIsWatching\":{\"10001\":true,\"10002\":false,\"10005\":true}}"
```

<h3 id="get-is-watching-issue-bulk-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful|[BulkIssueIsWatching](#schemabulkissueiswatching)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Get issue watchers

<a id="opIdgetIssueWatchers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/issue/string/watchers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/watchers`

Returns the watchers for an issue.

This operation requires the **Allow users to watch issues** option to be *ON*. This option is set in General configuration for Jira. See [Configuring Jira application options](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/uYXKM) for details.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is ini
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
 *  To see details of users on the watchlist other than themselves, *View voters and watchers* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.

<h3 id="get-issue-watchers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key of the issue.|


|404|Not Found|Returned if the issue is not found or the user does not have permission to view it.|None|

<aside class="warning">
