  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /rest/api/3/workflow/{entityId}`

Deletes a workflow.

The workflow cannot be deleted if it is:

 *  an active workflow.
 *  a system workflow.
 *  associated with any workflow scheme.
 *  associated with any draft workflow scheme.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-workflow-transition-rules">Workflow transition rules</h1>

This resource represents workflow transition rules. Workflow transition rules define a Connect app routine, such as a [workflow post functions](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/modules/workflow-post-function/) that is executed in association with the workflow. Use it to read and modify configuration of workflow transition rules.

## Get workflow transition rule configurations

<a id="opIdgetWorkflowTransitionRuleConfigurations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/rest/api/3/workflow/rule/config?types=postfunction' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/workflow/rule/config`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of workflows with transition rules. The workflows can be filtered to return only those containing workflow transition rules:

 *  of one or more transition rule types, such as [workflow post functions](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/modules/workflow-post-function/).
 *  matching one or more transition rule keys.

Only workflows containing transition rules created by the calling Connect app are returned.

Due to server-side optimizations, workflows with an empty list of rules may be returned; these workflows can be ignored.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Only Connect apps can use this operation.

<h3 id="get-workflow-transition-rule-configurations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|types|query|[string]|true|The types of the transition rules to return.|
|keys|query|[string]|false|The transition rule class keys, as defined in the Connect app descriptor, of the transition rules to return.|
|workflowNames|query|[string]|false|EXPERIMENTAL: The list of workflow names to filter by.|
|withTags|query|[string]|false|EXPERIMENTAL: The list of `tags` to filter by.|
|draft|query|boolean|false|EXPERIMENTAL: Whether draft or published workflows are returned. If not provided, both workflow types are returned.|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information in the response. This parameter accepts `transition`, which, for each rule, returns information about the transition the rule is assigned to.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|types|postfunction|
|types|condition|
|types|validator|

`PUT /rest/api/3/workflow/rule/config`

Updates configuration of workflow transition rules. The following rule types are supported:

 *  [post functions](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/modules/workflow-post-function/)
 *  [conditions](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/modules/workflow-condition/)
 *  [validators](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/modules/workflow-validator/)

Only rules created by the calling Connect app can be updated.

To assist with app migration, this operation can be used to:

 *  Disable a rule.
 *  Add a `tag`. Use this to filter rules in the [Get workflow transition rule configurations](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-workflow-transition-rules/#api-rest-api-3-workflow-rule-config-get).

Rules are enabled if the `disabled` parameter is not provided.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Only Connect apps can use this operation.

        }

          },

      ],
      "workflowId": {
        "draft": false,
        "name": "My Workflow name"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-workflow-schemes">Workflow schemes</h1>

This resource represents workflow schemes. Use it to manage workflow schemes and the workflow scheme's workflows and issue types.

A workflow scheme maps issue types to workflows. A workflow scheme can be associated with one or more projects, which enables the projects to use the workflow-issue type mappings.

Active workflow schemes (workflow schemes that are used by projects) cannot be edited. When an active workflow scheme is edited, a draft copy of the scheme is created. The draft workflow scheme is then be edited and published (replacing the active scheme).

See [Configuring workflow schemes](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/tohKLg) for more information.

## Get all workflow schemes

<a id="opIdgetAllWorkflowSchemes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/workflowscheme \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/workflowscheme`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of all workflow schemes, not including draft workflow schemes.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="get-all-workflow-schemes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"maxResults\":50,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":2,\"isLast\":true,\"values\":[{\"id\":101010,\"name\":\"Example workflow scheme\",\"description\":\"The description of the example workflow scheme.\",\"defaultWorkflow\":\"jira\",\"issueTypeMappings\":{\"10000\":\"scrum workflow\",\"10001\":\"builds workflow\"},\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/workflowscheme/101010\"},{\"id\":101011,\"name\":\"Another example workflow scheme\",\"description\":\"The description of the another example workflow scheme.\",\"defaultWorkflow\":\"jira\",\"issueTypeMappings\":{\"10000\":\"scrum workflow\",\"10001\":\"builds workflow\"},\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/workflowscheme/101011\"}]}"
```

## Create workflow scheme

<a id="opIdcreateWorkflowScheme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/workflowscheme \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "defaultWorkflow": "jira",
    "description": "The description of the example workflow scheme.",
    "issueTypeMappings": {
      "10000": "scrum workflow",
      "10001": "builds workflow"
    },
    "name": "Example workflow scheme"
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/workflowscheme`

Creates a workflow scheme.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "defaultWorkflow": "jira",
  "description": "The description of the example workflow scheme.",
  "issueTypeMappings": {
    "10000": "scrum workflow",
    "10001": "builds workflow"
  },
  "name": "Example workflow scheme"
}
```

<h3 id="create-workflow-scheme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[WorkflowScheme](#schemaworkflowscheme)|true|none|
|» defaultWorkflow|body|string|false|The name of the default workflow for the workflow scheme. The default workflow has *All Unassigned Issue Types* assigned to it in Jira. If `defaultWorkflow` is not specified when creating a workflow scheme, it is set to *Jira Workflow (jira)*.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the workflow scheme.|
|» issueTypeMappings|body|object|false|The issue type to workflow mappings, where each mapping is an issue type ID and workflow name pair. Note that an issue type can only be mapped to one workflow in a workflow scheme.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the workflow scheme. The name must be unique. The maximum length is 255 characters. Required when creating a workflow scheme.|
|» updateDraftIfNeeded|body|boolean|false|Whether to create or update a draft workflow scheme when updating an active workflow scheme. An active workflow scheme is a workflow scheme that is used by at least one project. The following examples show how this property works:<br><br> *  Update an active workflow scheme with `updateDraftIfNeeded` set to `true`: If a draft workflow scheme exists, it is updated. Otherwise, a draft workflow scheme is created.<br> *  Update an active workflow scheme with `updateDraftIfNeeded` set to `false`: An error is returned, as active workflow schemes cannot be updated.<br> *  Update an inactive workflow scheme with `updateDraftIfNeeded` set to `true`: The workflow scheme is updated, as inactive workflow schemes do not require drafts to update.<br><br>Defaults to `false`.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
"{\"id\":101010,\"name\":\"Example workflow scheme\",\"description\":\"The description of the example workflow scheme.\",\"defaultWorkflow\":\"jira\",\"issueTypeMappings\":{\"10000\":\"scrum workflow\",\"10001\":\"builds workflow\"},\"draft\":false,\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/workflowscheme/101010\"}"
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|201|Created|Returned if the request is successful.|[WorkflowScheme](#schemaworkflowscheme)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|

## Update workflow scheme

<a id="opIdupdateWorkflowScheme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/workflowscheme/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "defaultWorkflow": "jira",
    "description": "The description of the example workflow scheme.",
    "issueTypeMappings": {
      "10000": "scrum workflow"
    },
    "name": "Example workflow scheme",
    "updateDraftIfNeeded": false
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/workflowscheme/{id}`

Updates a workflow scheme, including the name, default workflow, issue type to project mappings, and more. If the workflow scheme is active (that is, being used by at least one project), then a draft workflow scheme is created or updated instead, provided that `updateDraftIfNeeded` is set to `true`.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "defaultWorkflow": "jira",
  "description": "The description of the example workflow scheme.",
  "issueTypeMappings": {
    "10000": "scrum workflow"
  },
  "name": "Example workflow scheme",
  "updateDraftIfNeeded": false
}
```

<h3 id="update-workflow-scheme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the workflow scheme. Find this ID by editing the desired workflow scheme in Jira. The ID is shown in the URL as `schemeId`. For example, *schemeId=10301*.|
|body|body|[WorkflowScheme](#schemaworkflowscheme)|true|none|
|» defaultWorkflow|body|string|false|The name of the default workflow for the workflow scheme. The default workflow has *All Unassigned Issue Types* assigned to it in Jira. If `defaultWorkflow` is not specified when creating a workflow scheme, it is set to *Jira Workflow (jira)*.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the workflow scheme.|
|» issueTypeMappings|body|object|false|The issue type to workflow mappings, where each mapping is an issue type ID and workflow name pair. Note that an issue type can only be mapped to one workflow in a workflow scheme.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the workflow scheme. The name must be unique. The maximum length is 255 characters. Required when creating a workflow scheme.|
|» updateDraftIfNeeded|body|boolean|false|Whether to create or update a draft workflow scheme when updating an active workflow scheme. An active workflow scheme is a workflow scheme that is used by at least one project. The following examples show how this property works:<br><br> *  Update an active workflow scheme with `updateDraftIfNeeded` set to `true`: If a draft workflow scheme exists, it is updated. Otherwise, a draft workflow scheme is created.<br> *  Update an active workflow scheme with `updateDraftIfNeeded` set to `false`: An error is returned, as active workflow schemes cannot be updated.<br> *  Update an inactive workflow scheme with `updateDraftIfNeeded` set to `true`: The workflow scheme is updated, as inactive workflow schemes do not require drafts to update.<br><br>Defaults to `false`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"id\":101010,\"name\":\"Example workflow scheme\",\"description\":\"The description of the example workflow scheme.\",\"defaultWorkflow\":\"jira\",\"issueTypeMappings\":{\"10000\":\"scrum workflow\",\"10001\":\"builds workflow\"},\"draft\":false,\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/workflowscheme/101010\"}"
```

<h3 id="update-workflow-scheme-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[WorkflowScheme](#schemaworkflowscheme)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the workflow scheme is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

`PUT /rest/api/3/workflowscheme/{id}/default`

Sets the default workflow for a workflow scheme.

Note that active workflow schemes cannot be edited. If the workflow scheme is active, set `updateDraftIfNeeded` to `true` in the request object and a draft workflow scheme is created or updated with the new default workflow. The draft workflow scheme can be published in Jira.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

{
  "updateDraftIfNeeded": false,
  "workflow": "jira"

|id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the workflow scheme.|
|body|body|[DefaultWorkflow](#schemadefaultworkflow)|true|The new default workflow.|
|» updateDraftIfNeeded|body|boolean|false|Whether a draft workflow scheme is created or updated when updating an active workflow scheme. The draft is updated with the new default workflow. Defaults to `false`.|
|» workflow|body|string|true|The name of the workflow to set as the default workflow.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"id\":101010,\"name\":\"Example workflow scheme\",\"description\":\"The description of the example workflow scheme.\",\"defaultWorkflow\":\"jira\",\"issueTypeMappings\":{\"10000\":\"scrum workflow\",\"10001\":\"builds workflow\"},\"draft\":false,\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/workflowscheme/101010\"}"
```

<h3 id="update-default-workflow-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[WorkflowScheme](#schemaworkflowscheme)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the workflow scheme cannot be edited and `updateDraftIfNeeded` is not `true`.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the workflow scheme is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )

```

`DELETE /rest/api/3/workflowscheme/{id}/workflow`

Deletes the workflow-issue type mapping for a workflow in a workflow scheme.

Note that active workflow schemes cannot be edited. If the workflow scheme is active, set `updateDraftIfNeeded` to `true` and a draft workflow scheme is created or updated with the workflow-issue type mapping deleted. The draft workflow scheme can be published in Jira.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the workflow scheme.|
|workflowName|query|string|true|The name of the workflow.|
|updateDraftIfNeeded|query|boolean|false|Set to true to create or update the draft of a workflow scheme and delete the mapping from the draft, when the workflow scheme cannot be edited. Defaults to `false`.|

<h3 id="delete-issue-types-for-workflow-in-workflow-scheme-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|None|

|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if any of the following is true:<br><br> *  The workflow scheme is not found.<br> *  The workflow is not found.<br> *  The workflow is not specified.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-workflow-scheme-project-associations">Workflow scheme project associations</h1>

This resource represents the associations between workflow schemes and projects.

For more information, see [Managing your workflows](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/q4hKLg).

## Get workflow scheme project associations

<a id="opIdgetWorkflowSchemeProjectAssociations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/rest/api/3/workflowscheme/project?projectId=10010' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/workflowscheme/project`

Returns a list of the workflow schemes associated with a list of projects. Each returned workflow scheme includes a list of the requested projects associated with it. Any team-managed or non-existent projects in the request are ignored and no errors are returned.

If the project is associated with the `Default Workflow Scheme` no ID is returned. This is because the way the `Default Workflow Scheme` is stored means it has no ID.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="get-workflow-scheme-project-associations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|query|[integer(int64)]|true|The ID of a project to return the workflow schemes for. To include multiple projects, provide an ampersand-Jim: oneseparated list. For example, `projectId=10000&projectId=10001`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"values\":[{\"projectIds\":[\"10010\",\"10020\"],\"workflowScheme\":{\"id\":101010,\"name\":\"Example workflow scheme\",\"description\":\"The description of the example workflow scheme.\",\"defaultWorkflow\":\"jira\",\"issueTypeMappings\":{\"10000\":\"scrum workflow\",\"10001\":\"builds workflow\"},\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/workflowscheme/101010\"}}]}"
```

> 400 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[],\"errors\":{\"projectId\":\"The ID of a project has to be provided.\"}}"
```

> 403 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"Only Jira administrators can access workflow scheme associations.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

<h3 id="get-workflow-scheme-project-associations-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[ContainerOfWorkflowSchemeAssociations](#schemacontainerofworkflowschemeassociations)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-workflow-scheme-drafts">Workflow scheme drafts</h1>

This resource represents draft workflow schemes. Use it to manage drafts of workflow schemes.

A workflow scheme maps issue types to workflows. A workflow scheme can be associated with one or more projects, which enables the projects to use the workflow-issue type mappings.

Active workflow schemes (workflow schemes that are used by projects) cannot be edited. Editing an active workflow scheme creates a draft copy of the scheme. The draft workflow scheme can then be edited and published (replacing the active scheme).

See [Configuring workflow schemes](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/tohKLg) for more information.

## Create draft workflow scheme

<a id="opIdcreateWorkflowSchemeDraftFromParent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/workflowscheme/0/createdraft \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /rest/api/3/workflowscheme/{id}/createdraft`

Create a draft workflow scheme from an active workflow scheme, by copying the active workflow scheme. Note that an active workflow scheme can only have one draft workflow scheme.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="create-draft-workflow-scheme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the active workflow scheme that the draft is created from.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json

## Get draft workflow scheme

<a id="opIdgetWorkflowSchemeDraft"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/workflowscheme/0/draft \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/workflowscheme/{id}/draft`

Returns the draft workflow scheme for an active workflow scheme. Draft workflow schemes allow changes to be made to the active workflow schemes: When an active workflow scheme is updated, a draft copy is created. The draft is modified, then the changes in the draft are copied back to the active workflow scheme. See [Configuring workflow schemes](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/tohKLg) for more information.  
Note that:

 *  Only active workflow schemes can have draft workflow schemes.
 *  An active workflow scheme can only have one draft workflow scheme.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="get-draft-workflow-scheme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the active workflow scheme that the draft was created from.|

## Update draft workflow scheme

<a id="opIdupdateWorkflowSchemeDraft"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/workflowscheme/0/draft \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "defaultWorkflow": "jira",
    "description": "The description of the example workflow scheme.",
    "issueTypeMappings": {
      "10000": "scrum workflow"
    },
    "name": "Example workflow scheme",
    "updateDraftIfNeeded": false
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/workflowscheme/{id}/draft`

Updates a draft workflow scheme. If a draft workflow scheme does not exist for the active workflow scheme, then a draft is created. Note that an active workflow scheme can only have one draft workflow scheme.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "defaultWorkflow": "jira",
  "description": "The description of the example workflow scheme.",
  "issueTypeMappings": {
    "10000": "scrum workflow"
  },
  "name": "Example workflow scheme",
  "updateDraftIfNeeded": false
}
```

<h3 id="update-draft-workflow-scheme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the active workflow scheme that the draft was created from.|
|body|body|[WorkflowScheme](#schemaworkflowscheme)|true|none|
|» defaultWorkflow|body|string|false|The name of the default workflow for the workflow scheme. The default workflow has *All Unassigned Issue Types* assigned to it in Jira. If `defaultWorkflow` is not specified when creating a workflow scheme, it is set to *Jira Workflow (jira)*.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the workflow scheme.|
|» issueTypeMappings|body|object|false|The issue type to workflow mappings, where each mapping is an issue type ID and workflow name pair. Note that an issue type can only be mapped to one workflow in a workflow scheme.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the workflow scheme. The name must be unique. The maximum length is 255 characters. Required when creating a workflow scheme.|
|» updateDraftIfNeeded|body|boolean|false|Whether to create or update a draft workflow scheme when updating an active workflow scheme. An active workflow scheme is a workflow scheme that is used by at least one project. The following examples show how this property works:<br><br> *  Update an active workflow scheme with `updateDraftIfNeeded` set to `true`: If a draft workflow scheme exists, it is updated. Otherwise, a draft workflow scheme is created.<br> *  Update an active workflow scheme with `updateDraftIfNeeded` set to `false`: An error is returned, as active workflow schemes cannot be updated.<br> *  Update an inactive workflow scheme with `updateDraftIfNeeded` set to `true`: The workflow scheme is updated, as inactive workflow schemes do not require drafts to update.<br><br>Defaults to `false`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"id\":17218781,\"name\":\"Example workflow scheme\",\"description\":\"The description of the example workflow scheme.\",\"defaultWorkflow\":\"scrum workflow\",\"issueTypeMappings\":{\"10000\":\"jira\",\"10001\":\"jira\"},\"originalDefaultWorkflow\":\"jira\",\"originalIssueTypeMappings\":{\"10001\":\"builds workflow\"},\"draft\":true,\"lastModifiedUser\":{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/user?accountId=5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"key\":\"\",\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"accountType\":\"atlassian\",\"name\":\"\",\"emailAddress\":\"mia@example.com\",\"avatarUrls\":{\"48x48\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=48&s=48\",\"24x24\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=24&s=24\",\"16x16\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=16&s=16\",\"32x32\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=32&s=32\"},\"displayName\":\"Mia Krystof\",\"active\":true,\"timeZone\":\"Australia/Sydney\",\"groups\":{\"size\":3,\"items\":[]},\"applicationRoles\":{\"size\":1,\"items\":[]}},\"lastModified\":\"Today 6:38 PM\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/workflowscheme/17218781/draft\"}"
```

## Publish draft workflow scheme

<a id="opIdpublishDraftWorkflowScheme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/workflowscheme/0/draft/publish \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "statusMappings": [
      {
        "issueTypeId": "10001",
        "newStatusId": "1",
        "statusId": "3"
      },
      {
        "issueTypeId": "10001",
        "newStatusId": "2",
        "statusId": "2"
      },
      {
        "issueTypeId": "10002",
        "newStatusId": "10003",
        "statusId": "10005"
      },
      {
        "issueTypeId": "10003",
        "newStatusId": "1",
        "statusId": "4"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/workflowscheme/{id}/draft/publish`

Publishes a draft workflow scheme.

Where the draft workflow includes new workflow statuses for an issue type, mappings are provided to update issues with the original workflow status to the new workflow status.

This operation is [asynchronous](#async). Follow the `location` link in the response to determine the status of the task and use [Get task](#api-rest-api-3-task-taskId-get) to obtain updates.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "statusMappings": [
    {
      "issueTypeId": "10001",
      "newStatusId": "1",
      "statusId": "3"
    },
    {
      "issueTypeId": "10001",
      "newStatusId": "2",
      "statusId": "2"
    },
    {
      "issueTypeId": "10002",
      "newStatusId": "10003",
      "statusId": "10005"
    },
    {
      "issueTypeId": "10003",
      "newStatusId": "1",
      "statusId": "4"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="publish-draft-workflow-scheme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the workflow scheme that the draft belongs to.|
|validateOnly|query|boolean|false|Whether the request only performs a validation.|
|body|body|[PublishDraftWorkflowScheme](#schemapublishdraftworkflowscheme)|true|Details of the status mappings.|
|» statusMappings|body|[[StatusMapping](#schemastatusmapping)]|false|Mappings of statuses to new statuses for issue types.|

> Example responses

> 303 Response

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "elapsedRuntime": 0,
  "finished": 0,
  "id": "string",
  "lastUpdate": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "progress": 0,
  "result": null,
  "self": "http://example.com",
  "started": 0,
  "status": "ENQUEUED",
  "submitted": 0,
  "submittedBy": 0
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"Issue type with ID '2','4' is missing the mappings required for statuses with IDs 10004.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 404 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"Draft workflow scheme was not found.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

<h3 id="publish-draft-workflow-scheme-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the request is only for validation and is successful.|None|
|303|See Other|Returned if the request is successful.|[TaskProgressBeanObject](#schemataskprogressbeanobject)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if any of these are true:<br><br> *  The workflow scheme is not found.<br> *  The workflow scheme does not have a draft.<br> *  A new status in the draft workflow scheme is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-workflow-statuses">Workflow statuses</h1>

This resource represents issue workflow statuses. Use it to obtain a list of all statuses associated with workflows and the details of a status.

## Get all statuses

<a id="opIdgetStatuses"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/status \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/status`

Returns a list of all statuses associated with active workflows.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** None.

"[{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/status/10000\",\"description\":\"The issue is currently being worked on.\",\"iconUrl\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/images/icons/progress.gif\",\"name\":\"In Progress\",\"id\":\"10000\",\"statusCategory\":{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/statuscategory/1\",\"id\":1,\"key\":\"in-flight\",\"colorName\":\"yellow\",\"name\":\"In Progress\"}},{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/status/5\",\"description\":\"The issue is closed.\",\"iconUrl\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/images/icons/closed.gif\",\"name\":\"Closed\",\"id\":\"5\",\"statusCategory\":{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/statuscategory/9\",\"id\":9,\"key\":\"completed\",\"colorName\":\"green\"}}]"

## Get status

<a id="opIdgetStatus"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/api/3/status/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/status/{idOrName}`

Returns a status. The status must be associated with an active workflow to be returned.

If a name is used on more than one status, only the status found first is returned. Therefore, identifying the status by its ID may be preferable.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

[Permissions](#permissions) required: None.

<h3 id="get-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idOrName|path|string|true|The ID or name of the status.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/status/10000\",\"description\":\"The issue is currently being worked on.\",\"iconUrl\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/images/icons/progress.gif\",\"name\":\"In Progress\",\"id\":\"10000\",\"statusCategory\":{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/statuscategory/1\",\"id\":1,\"key\":\"in-flight\",\"colorName\":\"yellow\",\"name\":\"In Progress\"}}"
```

<h3 id="get-status-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[StatusDetails](#schemastatusdetails)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if:<br><br> *  the status is not found.<br> *  the status is not associated with a workflow.<br> *  the user does not have the required permissions.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-workflow-status-categories">Workflow status categories</h1>

This resource represents status categories. Use it to obtain a list of all status categories and the details of a category. Status categories provided a mechanism for categorizing [statuses](#api-group-Workflow-statuses).

```

`GET /rest/api/3/statuscategory`

Returns a list of all status categories.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Permission to access Jira.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

"[{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/statuscategory/1\",\"id\":1,\"key\":\"in-flight\",\"colorName\":\"yellow\",\"name\":\"In Progress\"},{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/statuscategory/9\",\"id\":9,\"key\":\"completed\",\"colorName\":\"green\"}]"

<h3 id="get-all-status-categories-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|*anonymous*|[[StatusCategory](#schemastatuscategory)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-workflow-transition-properties">Workflow transition properties</h1>

This resource represents workflow transition properties, which provides for storing custom data against a workflow transition. Use it to get, create, and delete workflow transition properties as well as get a list of property keys for a workflow transition. Workflow transition properties are a type of [entity property](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/jira-entity-properties/).

## Get workflow transition properties

<a id="opIdgetWorkflowTransitionProperties"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/rest/api/3/workflow/transitions/0/properties?workflowName=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/workflow/transitions/{transitionId}/properties`

Returns the properties on a workflow transition. Transition properties are used to change the behavior of a transition. For more information, see [Transition properties](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/zIhKLg#Advancedworkflowconfiguration-transitionproperties) and [Workflow properties](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/JYlKLg).

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="get-workflow-transition-properties-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transitionId|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the transition. To get the ID, view the workflow in text mode in the Jira administration console. The ID is shown next to the transition.|
|includeReservedKeys|query|boolean|false|Some properties with keys that have the *jira.* prefix are reserved, which means they are not editable. To include these properties in the results, set this parameter to *true*.|
|key|query|string|false|The key of the property being returned, also known as the name of the property. If this parameter is not specified, all properties on the transition are returned.|
|workflowName|query|string|true|The name of the workflow that the transition belongs to.|
|workflowMode|query|string|false|The workflow status. Set to *live* for active and inactive workflows, or *draft* for draft workflows.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|workflowMode|live|
|workflowMode|draft|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"[{\"key\":\"jira.i18n.title\",\"value\":\"some.title\",\"id\":\"jira.i18n.title\"},{\"key\":\"jira.permission\",\"value\":\"createissue\",\"id\":\"jira.permission\"}]"
```

<h3 id="get-workflow-transition-properties-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|200 response|[WorkflowTransitionProperty](#schemaworkflowtransitionproperty)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have admin permission|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the workflow transition or property is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

## Update workflow transition property

<a id="opIdupdateWorkflowTransitionProperty"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/rest/api/3/workflow/transitions/0/properties?key=string&workflowName=string' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "value": "createissue"
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/workflow/transitions/{transitionId}/properties`

Updates a workflow transition by changing the property value. Trying to update a property that does not exist results in a new property being added to the transition. Transition properties are used to change the behavior of a transition. For more information, see [Transition properties](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/zIhKLg#Advancedworkflowconfiguration-transitionproperties) and [Workflow properties](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/JYlKLg).

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "value": "createissue"
}
```

<h3 id="update-workflow-transition-property-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transitionId|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the transition. To get the ID, view the workflow in text mode in the Jira admin settings. The ID is shown next to the transition.|
|key|query|string|true|The key of the property being updated, also known as the name of the property. Set this to the same value as the `key` defined in the request body.|
|workflowName|query|string|true|The name of the workflow that the transition belongs to.|
|workflowMode|query|string|false|The workflow status. Set to `live` for inactive workflows or `draft` for draft workflows. Active workflows cannot be edited.|
|body|body|[WorkflowTransitionProperty](#schemaworkflowtransitionproperty)|true|none|
|» value|body|string|true|The value of the transition property.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|workflowMode|live|
|workflowMode|draft|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"key\":\"jira.i18n.title\",\"value\":\"some.title\",\"id\":\"jira.i18n.title\"}"
```

<h3 id="update-workflow-transition-property-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|200 response|[WorkflowTransitionProperty](#schemaworkflowtransitionproperty)|
|304|Not Modified|Returned if no changes were made by the request. For example, attempting to update a property with its current value.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the workflow transition is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

## Create workflow transition property

<a id="opIdcreateWorkflowTransitionProperty"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/rest/api/3/workflow/transitions/0/properties?key=string&workflowName=string' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "value": "createissue"
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/workflow/transitions/{transitionId}/properties`

Adds a property to a workflow transition. Transition properties are used to change the behavior of a transition. For more information, see [Transition properties](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/zIhKLg#Advancedworkflowconfiguration-transitionproperties) and [Workflow properties](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/JYlKLg).

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "value": "createissue"
}
```

<h3 id="create-workflow-transition-property-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transitionId|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the transition. To get the ID, view the workflow in text mode in the Jira admin settings. The ID is shown next to the transition.|
|key|query|string|true|The key of the property being added, also known as the name of the property. Set this to the same value as the `key` defined in the request body.|
|workflowName|query|string|true|The name of the workflow that the transition belongs to.|
|workflowMode|query|string|false|The workflow status. Set to *live* for inactive workflows or *draft* for draft workflows. Active workflows cannot be edited.|
|body|body|[WorkflowTransitionProperty](#schemaworkflowtransitionproperty)|true|none|
|» value|body|string|true|The value of the transition property.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|workflowMode|live|
|workflowMode|draft|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"key\":\"jira.i18n.title\",\"value\":\"some.title\",\"id\":\"jira.i18n.title\"}"
```

<h3 id="create-workflow-transition-property-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|200 response|[WorkflowTransitionProperty](#schemaworkflowtransitionproperty)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if a workflow property with the same key is present on the transition.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the workflow transition is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

## Delete workflow transition property

<a id="opIddeleteWorkflowTransitionProperty"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/rest/api/3/workflow/transitions/0/properties?key=string&workflowName=string' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /rest/api/3/workflow/transitions/{transitionId}/properties`

Deletes a property from a workflow transition. Transition properties are used to change the behavior of a transition. For more information, see [Transition properties](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/zIhKLg#Advancedworkflowconfiguration-transitionproperties) and [Workflow properties](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/JYlKLg).

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="delete-workflow-transition-property-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transitionId|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the transition. To get the ID, view the workflow in text mode in the Jira admin settings. The ID is shown next to the transition.|
|key|query|string|true|The name of the transition property to delete, also known as the name of the property.|
|workflowName|query|string|true|The name of the workflow that the transition belongs to.|
|workflowMode|query|string|false|The workflow status. Set to `live` for inactive workflows or `draft` for draft workflows. Active workflows cannot be edited.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|workflowMode|live|
|workflowMode|draft|

<h3 id="delete-workflow-transition-property-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|200 response|None|
|304|Not Modified|Returned if no changes were made by the request. For example, trying to delete a property that cannot be found.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the workflow transition is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-app-properties">App properties</h1>

This resource represents app properties. Use it to store arbitrary data for your
[Connect app](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/index/#connect-apps).

## Get app properties

<a id="opIdAddonPropertiesResource.getAddonProperties_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/atlassian-connect/1/addons/string/properties \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/atlassian-connect/1/addons/{addonKey}/properties`

Gets all the properties of an app.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Only a Connect app whose key matches `addonKey` can make this request.
Additionally, Forge apps published on the Marketplace can access properties of Connect apps they were [migrated from](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/build-a-connect-on-forge-app/).

<h3 id="get-app-properties-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|addonKey|path|string|true|The key of the app, as defined in its descriptor.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "keys": [
    {
      "key": "propertyKey",
      "self": "https://your-domain.atlassian.net/jira/rest/atlassian-connect/1/addon/example.app.key/properties/propertyKey"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Access to this resource must be authenticated as an app.",
  "statusCode": 401
}
```

<h3 id="get-app-properties-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PropertyKeys](#schemapropertykeys)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|[OperationMessage](#schemaoperationmessage)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2
</aside>

## Get app property

<a id="opIdAddonPropertiesResource.getAddonProperty_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/atlassian-connect/1/addons/string/properties/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/atlassian-connect/1/addons/{addonKey}/properties/{propertyKey}`

Returns the key and value of an app's property.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Only a Connect app whose key matches `addonKey` can make this request.
Additionally, Forge apps published on the Marketplace can access properties of Connect apps they were [migrated from](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/build-a-connect-on-forge-app/).

<h3 id="get-app-property-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|addonKey|path|string|true|The key of the app, as defined in its descriptor.|
|propertyKey|path|string|true|The key of the property.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "key": "propertyKey",
  "self": "https://your-domain.atlassian.net/jira/rest/atlassian-connect/1/addon/example.app.key/properties/propertyKey",
  "value": "propertyValue"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "The property key cannot be longer than 127 characters.",
  "statusCode": 400
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Access to this resource must be authenticated as an app.",
  "statusCode": 401
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Property with key not found.",
  "statusCode": 404
}
```

<h3 id="get-app-property-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[EntityProperty](#schemaentityproperty)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the property key is longer than 127 characters.|[OperationMessage](#schemaoperationmessage)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|[OperationMessage](#schemaoperationmessage)|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the property is not found or doesn't belong to the app.|[OperationMessage](#schemaoperationmessage)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2
</aside>

## Set app property

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/atlassian-connect/1/addons/string/properties/string \

  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'null'
```

`PUT /rest/atlassian-connect/1/addons/{addonKey}/properties/{propertyKey}`

Sets the value of an app's property. Use this resource to store custom data for your app.

The value of the request body must be a [valid](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4627), non-empty JSON blob. The maximum length is 32768 characters.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Only a Connect app whose key matches `addonKey` can make this request.

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="set-app-property-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|addonKey|path|string|true|The key of the app, as defined in its descriptor.|
|propertyKey|path|string|true|The key of the property.|
|body|body|object|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Property updated.",
  "statusCode": 200
}
```

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Property created.",
  "statusCode": 201
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "The property key cannot be longer than 127 characters.",
  "statusCode": 400
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Access to this resource must be authenticated as an app.",
  "statusCode": 401
}
```

<h3 id="set-app-property-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the property is updated.|[OperationMessage](#schemaoperationmessage)|
|201|Created|Returned is the property is created.|[OperationMessage](#schemaoperationmessage)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if:<br>  * the property key is longer than 127 characters.<br>  * the value is not valid JSON.<br>  * the value is longer than 32768 characters.|[OperationMessage](#schemaoperationmessage)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|[OperationMessage](#schemaoperationmessage)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-dynamic-modules">Dynamic modules</h1>

This resource represents [modules registered dynamically](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/dynamic-modules/)
by [Connect apps](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/index/#connect-apps).

## Get modules

<a id="opIdDynamicModulesResource.getModules_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/atlassian-connect/1/app/module/dynamic \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /rest/atlassian-connect/1/app/module/dynamic`

Returns all modules registered dynamically by the calling app.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Only Connect apps can make this request.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "jiraEntityProperties": [
    {
      "entityType": "issue",
      "key": "dynamic-attachment-entity-property",
      "keyConfigurations": [
        {
          "extractions": [
            {
              "alias": "attachmentExtension",
              "objectName": "extension",
              "type": "text"
            }
          ],
          "propertyKey": "attachment"
        }
      ],
      "name": {
        "value": "Attachment Index Document"
      }
    }
  ],
  "jiraIssueFields": [
    {
      "description": {
        "value": "A dynamically added single-select field"
      },
      "extractions": [
        {
          "name": "categoryName",
          "path": "category",
          "type": "text"
        }
      ],
      "key": "dynamic-select-field",
      "name": {
        "value": "Dynamic single select"
      },
      "type": "single_select"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "message": "The request is not from a Connect app."
}
```

<h3 id="get-modules-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

## Register modules

<a id="opIdDynamicModulesResource.registerModules_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/atlassian-connect/1/app/module/dynamic \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "jiraEntityProperties": [
      {
        "entityType": "issue",
        "key": "dynamic-attachment-entity-property",
        "keyConfigurations": [
          {
            "extractions": [
              {
                "alias": "attachmentExtension",
                "objectName": "extension",
                "type": "text"
              }
            ],
            "propertyKey": "attachment"
          }
        ],
        "name": {
          "value": "Attachment Index Document"
        }
      }
    ],
    "jiraIssueFields": [
      {
        "description": {
          "value": "A dynamically added single-select field"
        },
        "extractions": [
          {
            "name": "categoryName",
            "path": "category",
            "type": "text"
          }
        ],
        "key": "dynamic-select-field",
        "name": {
          "value": "Dynamic single select"
        },
        "type": "single_select"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /rest/atlassian-connect/1/app/module/dynamic`

Registers a list of modules.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Only Connect apps can make this request.

```json
{

        }

  "message": "Installation failed. The app com.example.app.key has duplicate module keys: [module-key]. Please contact the app vendor."

}

For example, required properties are missing.<br>* any of the modules conflict with registered dynamic modules or modules defined in the app descriptor. For example, there are duplicate keys.<br><br>Details of the issues encountered are included in the error message.|[ErrorMessage](#schemaerrormessage)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the call is not from a Connect app.|[ErrorMessage](#schemaerrormessage)|

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-app-migration">App migration</h1>

This resource supports [app migrations](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/app-migration/). Use it to:
- [to request migrated workflow rules details](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/app-migration/tutorials/migration-app-workflow-rules/).
- [perform bulk updates of entity properties](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/app-migration/tutorials/entity-properties-bulk-api/).
- [perform bulk updates of issue custom field values](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/app-migration/tutorials/migrating-app-custom-fields/).

## Bulk update custom field value

<a id="opIdAppIssueFieldValueUpdateResource.updateIssueFields_put"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/atlassian-connect/1/migration/field \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'Atlassian-Transfer-Id: 497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08' \
  -d '{
    "updateValueList": [
      {
        "_type": "StringIssueField",
        "fieldID": 10076,
        "issueID": 10001,
        "string": "new string value"
      },
      {
        "_type": "TextIssueField",
        "fieldID": 10077,
        "issueID": 10002,
        "text": "new text value"
      },
      {
        "_type": "SingleSelectIssueField",
        "fieldID": 10078,
        "issueID": 10003,
        "optionID": "1"
      },
      {
        "_type": "MultiSelectIssueField",
        "fieldID": 10079,
        "issueID": 10004,
        "optionID": "2"
      },
      {
        "_type": "RichTextIssueField",
        "fieldID": 10080,
        "issueID": 10005,
        "richText": "new rich text value"
      },
      {
        "_type": "NumberIssueField",
        "fieldID": 10082,
        "issueID": 10006,
        "number": 54
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/atlassian-connect/1/migration/field`

Updates the value of a custom field added by Connect apps on one or more issues.
The values of up to 200 custom fields can be updated.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Only Connect apps can make this request.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "updateValueList": [
    {
      "_type": "StringIssueField",
      "fieldID": 10076,
      "issueID": 10001,
      "string": "new string value"
    },
    {
      "_type": "TextIssueField",
      "fieldID": 10077,
      "issueID": 10002,
      "text": "new text value"
    },
    {
      "_type": "SingleSelectIssueField",
      "fieldID": 10078,
      "issueID": 10003,
      "optionID": "1"
    },
    {
      "_type": "MultiSelectIssueField",
      "fieldID": 10079,
      "issueID": 10004,
      "optionID": "2"
    },
    {
      "_type": "RichTextIssueField",
      "fieldID": 10080,
      "issueID": 10005,
      "richText": "new rich text value"
    },
    {
      "_type": "NumberIssueField",
      "fieldID": 10082,
      "issueID": 10006,
      "number": 54
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-update-custom-field-value-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Atlassian-Transfer-Id|header|string(uuid)|true|The ID of the transfer.|
|body|body|[ConnectCustomFieldValues](#schemaconnectcustomfieldvalues)|true|none|
|» updateValueList|body|[[ConnectCustomFieldValue](#schemaconnectcustomfieldvalue)]|false|The list of custom field update details.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="bulk-update-custom-field-value-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|

## Get workflow transition rule configurations

<a id="opIdMigrationResource.workflowRuleSearch_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rest/atlassian-connect/1/migration/workflow/rule/search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'Atlassian-Transfer-Id: 497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08' \
  -d '{
    "expand": "transition",
    "ruleIds": [
      "55d44f1d-c859-42e5-9c27-2c5ec3f340b1"
    ],
    "workflowEntityId": "a498d711-685d-428d-8c3e-bc03bb450ea7"
  }'
```

`POST /rest/atlassian-connect/1/migration/workflow/rule/search`

Returns configurations for workflow transition rules migrated from server to cloud and owned by the calling Connect app.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expand": "transition",
  "ruleIds": [
    "55d44f1d-c859-42e5-9c27-2c5ec3f340b1"
  ],
  "workflowEntityId": "a498d711-685d-428d-8c3e-bc03bb450ea7"
}

<h3 id="get-workflow-transition-rule-configurations-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|

|body|body|[WorkflowRulesSearch](#schemaworkflowrulessearch)|true|none|
|» expand|body|string|false|Use expand to include additional information in the response. This parameter accepts `transition` which, for each rule, returns information about the transition the rule is assigned to.|
|» ruleIds|body|[string(uuid)]|true|The list of workflow rule IDs.|
|» workflowEntityId|body|string(uuid)|true|The workflow ID.|

|id|string|false|read-only|The ID of the comment.|
|jsdAuthorCanSeeRequest|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the comment was added from an email sent by a person who is not part of the issue. See [Allow external emails to be added as comments on issues](https://support.atlassian.com/jira-service-management-cloud/docs/allow-external-emails-to-be-added-as-comments-on-issues/)for information on setting up this feature.|
|jsdPublic|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the comment is visible in Jira Service Desk. Defaults to true when comments are created in the Jira Cloud Platform. This includes when the site doesn't use Jira Service Desk or the project isn't a Jira Service Desk project and, therefore, there is no Jira Service Desk for the issue to be visible on. To create a comment with its visibility in Jira Service Desk set to false, use the Jira Service Desk REST API [Create request comment](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/service-desk/rest/#api-rest-servicedeskapi-request-issueIdOrKey-comment-post) operation.|
|properties|[[EntityProperty](#schemaentityproperty)]|false|none|A list of comment properties. Optional on create and update.|
|renderedBody|string|false|read-only|The rendered version of the comment.|
|self|string|false|read-only|The URL of the comment.|
|updateAuthor|object|false|read-only|The ID of the user who updated the comment last.|
|updated|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The date and time at which the comment was updated last.|
|visibility|object|false|none|The group or role to which this comment is visible. Optional on create and update.|

      "max-results": 0,
      "pagingCallback": {},
      "size": 0
    },
    "key": "string",
    "locale": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "self": "http://example.com",
    "timeZone": "string"
  },
  "realAssigneeType": "PROJECT_DEFAULT",
  "self": "http://example.com"
}
```

Details about a component with a count of the issues it contains.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assignee|object|false|none|The details of the user associated with `assigneeType`, if any. See `realAssignee` for details of the user assigned to issues created with this component.|
|assigneeType|string|false|read-only|The nominal user type used to determine the assignee for issues created with this component. See `realAssigneeType` for details on how the type of the user, and hence the user, assigned to issues is determined. Takes the following values:<br><br> *  `PROJECT_LEAD` the assignee to any issues created with this component is nominally the lead for the project the component is in.<br> *  `COMPONENT_LEAD` the assignee to any issues created with this component is nominally the lead for the component.<br> *  `UNASSIGNED` an assignee is not set for issues created with this component.<br> *  `PROJECT_DEFAULT` the assignee to any issues created with this component is nominally the default assignee for the project that the component is in.|
|description|string|false|read-only|The description for the component.|
|id|string|false|read-only|The unique identifier for the component.|
|isAssigneeTypeValid|boolean|false|read-only|Whether a user is associated with `assigneeType`. For example, if the `assigneeType` is set to `COMPONENT_LEAD` but the component lead is not set, then `false` is returned.|
|issueCount|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Count of issues for the component.|
|lead|object|false|none|The user details for the component's lead user.|
|name|string|false|read-only|The name for the component.|
|project|string|false|read-only|The key of the project to which the component is assigned.|
|projectId|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Not used.|
|realAssignee|object|false|none|The user assigned to issues created with this component, when `assigneeType` does not identify a valid assignee.|
|realAssigneeType|string|false|read-only|The type of the assignee that is assigned to issues created with this component, when an assignee cannot be set from the `assigneeType`. For example, `assigneeType` is set to `COMPONENT_LEAD` but no component lead is set. This property is set to one of the following values:<br><br> *  `PROJECT_LEAD` when `assigneeType` is `PROJECT_LEAD` and the project lead has permission to be assigned issues in the project that the component is in.<br> *  `COMPONENT_LEAD` when `assignee`Type is `COMPONENT_LEAD` and the component lead has permission to be assigned issues in the project that the component is in.<br> *  `UNASSIGNED` when `assigneeType` is `UNASSIGNED` and Jira is configured to allow unassigned issues.<br> *  `PROJECT_DEFAULT` when none of the preceding cases are true.|
|self|string(uri)|false|read-only|The URL for this count of the issues contained in the component.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|assigneeType|PROJECT_DEFAULT|
|assigneeType|COMPONENT_LEAD|
|assigneeType|PROJECT_LEAD|
|assigneeType|UNASSIGNED|
|realAssigneeType|PROJECT_DEFAULT|
|realAssigneeType|COMPONENT_LEAD|
|realAssigneeType|PROJECT_LEAD|
|realAssigneeType|UNASSIGNED|

<h2 id="tocS_CompoundClause">CompoundClause</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacompoundclause"></a>
<a id="schema_CompoundClause"></a>
<a id="tocScompoundclause"></a>
<a id="tocscompoundclause"></a>

```json
{
  "clauses": [
    {}
  ],
  "operator": "and"
}
```

A JQL query clause that consists of nested clauses. For example, `(labels in (urgent, blocker) OR lastCommentedBy = currentUser()). Note that, where nesting is not defined, the parser nests JQL clauses based on the operator precedence. For example, "A OR B AND C" is parsed as "(A OR B) AND C". See Setting the precedence of operators for more information about precedence in JQL queries.`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|clauses|[[JqlQueryClause](#schemajqlqueryclause)]|true|none|The list of nested clauses.|
|operator|string|true|none|The operator between the clauses.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|operator|and|
|operator|or|
|operator|not|

|watchingEnabled|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the ability for users to watch issues is enabled. See [Configuring Jira application options](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/uYXKM) for details.|

<h2 id="tocS_CustomFieldDefinitionJsonBean">CustomFieldDefinitionJsonBean</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacustomfielddefinitionjsonbean"></a>
<a id="schema_CustomFieldDefinitionJsonBean"></a>
<a id="tocScustomfielddefinitionjsonbean"></a>
<a id="tocscustomfielddefinitionjsonbean"></a>

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "searcherKey": "com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:cascadingselectsearcher",
  "type": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string|false|none|The description of the custom field, which is displayed in Jira.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the custom field, which is displayed in Jira. This is not the unique identifier.|
|searcherKey|string|false|none|The searcher defines the way the field is searched in Jira. For example, *com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:grouppickersearcher*.  <br>The search UI (basic search and JQL search) will display different operations and values for the field, based on the field searcher. You must specify a searcher that is valid for the field type, as listed below (abbreviated values shown):<br><br> *  `cascadingselect`: `cascadingselectsearcher`<br> *  `datepicker`: `daterange`<br> *  `datetime`: `datetimerange`<br> *  `float`: `exactnumber` or `numberrange`<br> *  `grouppicker`: `grouppickersearcher`<br> *  `importid`: `exactnumber` or `numberrange`<br> *  `labels`: `labelsearcher`<br> *  `multicheckboxes`: `multiselectsearcher`<br> *  `multigrouppicker`: `multiselectsearcher`<br> *  `multiselect`: `multiselectsearcher`<br> *  `multiuserpicker`: `userpickergroupsearcher`<br> *  `multiversion`: `versionsearcher`<br> *  `project`: `projectsearcher`<br> *  `radiobuttons`: `multiselectsearcher`<br> *  `readonlyfield`: `textsearcher`<br> *  `select`: `multiselectsearcher`<br> *  `textarea`: `textsearcher`<br> *  `textfield`: `textsearcher`<br> *  `url`: `exacttextsearcher`<br> *  `userpicker`: `userpickergroupsearcher`<br> *  `version`: `versionsearcher`<br><br>If no searcher is provided, the field isn't searchable. However, [Forge custom fields](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/manifest-reference/modules/#jira-custom-field-type--beta-) have a searcher set automatically, so are always searchable.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the custom field. These built-in custom field types are available:<br><br> *  `cascadingselect`: Enables values to be selected from two levels of select lists (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:cascadingselect`)<br> *  `datepicker`: Stores a date using a picker control (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:datepicker`)<br> *  `datetime`: Stores a date with a time component (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:datetime`)<br> *  `float`: Stores and validates a numeric (floating point) input (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:float`)<br> *  `grouppicker`: Stores a user group using a picker control (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:grouppicker`)<br> *  `importid`: A read-only field that stores the ID the issue had in the system it was imported from (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:importid`)<br> *  `labels`: Stores labels (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:labels`)<br> *  `multicheckboxes`: Stores multiple values using checkboxes (value: ``)<br> *  `multigrouppicker`: Stores multiple user groups using a picker control (value: ``)<br> *  `multiselect`: Stores multiple values using a select list (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:multicheckboxes`)<br> *  `multiuserpicker`: Stores multiple users using a picker control (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:multigrouppicker`)<br> *  `multiversion`: Stores multiple versions from the versions available in a project using a picker control (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:multiversion`)<br> *  `project`: Stores a project from a list of projects that the user is permitted to view (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:project`)<br> *  `radiobuttons`: Stores a value using radio buttons (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:radiobuttons`)<br> *  `readonlyfield`: Stores a read-only text value, which can only be populated via the API (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:readonlyfield`)<br> *  `select`: Stores a value from a configurable list of options (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:select`)<br> *  `textarea`: Stores a long text string using a multiline text area (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:textarea`)<br> *  `textfield`: Stores a text string using a single-line text box (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:textfield`)<br> *  `url`: Stores a URL (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:url`)<br> *  `userpicker`: Stores a user using a picker control (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:userpicker`)<br> *  `version`: Stores a version using a picker control (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:version`)<br><br>To create a field based on a [Forge custom field type](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/manifest-reference/modules/#jira-custom-field-type--beta-), use the ID of the Forge custom field type as the value. For example, `ari:cloud:ecosystem::extension/e62f20a2-4b61-4dbe-bfb9-9a88b5e3ac84/548c5df1-24aa-4f7c-bbbb-3038d947cb05/static/my-cf-type-key`.|

<h2 id="tocS_CustomFieldValueUpdate">CustomFieldValueUpdate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacustomfieldvalueupdate"></a>
<a id="schema_CustomFieldValueUpdate"></a>
<a id="tocScustomfieldvalueupdate"></a>
<a id="tocscustomfieldvalueupdate"></a>

```json
{
  "issueIds": [
    0
  ],
  "value": null
}
```

A list of issue IDs and the value to update a custom field to.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIds|[integer(int64)]|true|write-only|The list of issue IDs.|
|value|object|true|none|The value for the custom field. The value must be compatible with the [custom field type](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/manifest-reference/modules/jira-custom-field/#data-types) as follows:<br><br> *  `string` the value must be a string.<br> *  `number` the value must be a number.<br> *  `datetime` the value must be a string that represents a date in the ISO format or the simplified extended ISO format. For example, `"2023-01-18T12:00:00-03:00"` or `"2023-01-18T12:00:00.000Z"`. However, the milliseconds part is ignored.<br> *  `user` the value must be an object that contains the `accountId` field.<br> *  `group` the value must be an object that contains the group `name` or `groupId` field. Because group names can change, we recommend using `groupId`.<br><br>A list of appropriate values must be provided if the field is of the `list` [collection type](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/manifest-reference/modules/jira-custom-field/#collection-types).|

```

Details of a dashboard.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|automaticRefreshMs|integer(int32)|false|read-only|The automatic refresh interval for the dashboard in milliseconds.|
|description|string|false|none|none|
|editPermissions|[[SharePermission](#schemasharepermission)]|false|read-only|The details of any edit share permissions for the dashboard.|
|id|string|false|read-only|The ID of the dashboard.|
|isFavourite|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the dashboard is selected as a favorite by the user.|
|isWritable|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the current user has permission to edit the dashboard.|
|name|string|false|read-only|The name of the dashboard.|
|owner|object|false|read-only|The owner of the dashboard.|
|popularity|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The number of users who have this dashboard as a favorite.|
|rank|integer(int32)|false|read-only|The rank of this dashboard.|
|self|string(uri)|false|read-only|The URL of these dashboard details.|
|sharePermissions|[[SharePermission](#schemasharepermission)]|false|read-only|The details of any view share permissions for the dashboard.|
|systemDashboard|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the current dashboard is system dashboard.|
|view|string|false|read-only|The URL of the dashboard.|

<h2 id="tocS_DashboardGadgetSettings">DashboardGadgetSettings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadashboardgadgetsettings"></a>

<a id="tocSdashboardgadgetsettings"></a>
<a id="tocsdashboardgadgetsettings"></a>

```json
{
  "color": "string",
  "ignoreUriAndModuleKeyValidation": true,
  "moduleKey": "string",
  "position": {
    "The column position of the gadget.": 0,
    "The row position of the gadget.": 0
  },
  "title": "string",
  "uri": "string"
}
```

Details of the settings for a dashboard gadget.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|color|string|false|write-only|The color of the gadget. Should be one of `blue`, `red`, `yellow`, `green`, `cyan`, `purple`, `gray`, or `white`.|
|ignoreUriAndModuleKeyValidation|boolean|false|write-only|Whether to ignore the validation of module key and URI. For example, when a gadget is created that is a part of an application that isn't installed.|
|moduleKey|string|false|write-only|The module key of the gadget type. Can't be provided with `uri`.|
|position|object|false|none|The position of the gadget. When the gadget is placed into the position, other gadgets in the same column are moved down to accommodate it.|
|title|string|false|write-only|The title of the gadget.|
|uri|string|false|write-only|The URI of the gadget type. Can't be provided with `moduleKey`.|

Details of the scope of the default sharing for new filters and dashboards.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|scope|string|true|none|The scope of the default sharing for new filters and dashboards:<br><br> *  `AUTHENTICATED` Shared with all logged-in users.<br> *  `GLOBAL` Shared with all logged-in users. This shows as `AUTHENTICATED` in the response.<br> *  `PRIVATE` Not shared with any users.|
