```json
  "type": "TRACKED",
  "value": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

Information about the most recent use of a field.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|Last used value type:<br><br> *  *TRACKED*: field is tracked and a last used date is available.<br> *  *NOT\_TRACKED*: field is not tracked, last used date is not available.<br> *  *NO\_INFORMATION*: field is tracked, but no last used date is available.|
|value|string(date-time)|false|none|The date when the value of the field last changed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|TRACKED|
|type|NOT_TRACKED|
|type|NO_INFORMATION|

```json
{
```

```json
  "cfid": "string",
  "deprecated": "true",
  "deprecatedSearcherKey": "string",
  "displayName": "string",
  "operators": [
    "string"
  ],
  "orderable": "true",
  "searchable": "true",
  "types": [
    "string"
  ],
  "value": "string"
}
```

Details of a field that can be used in advanced searches.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|auto|string|false|none|Whether the field provide auto-complete suggestions.|
|cfid|string|false|none|If the item is a custom field, the ID of the custom field.|
|deprecated|string|false|none|Whether this field has been deprecated.|
|deprecatedSearcherKey|string|false|none|The searcher key of the field, only passed when the field is deprecated.|
|displayName|string|false|none|The display name contains the following:<br><br> *  for system fields, the field name. For example, `Summary`.<br> *  for collapsed custom fields, the field name followed by a hyphen and then the field name and field type. For example, `Component - Component[Dropdown]`.<br> *  for other custom fields, the field name followed by a hyphen and then the custom field ID. For example, `Component - cf[10061]`.|
|operators|[string]|false|none|The valid search operators for the field.|
|orderable|string|false|none|Whether the field can be used in a query's `ORDER BY` clause.|
|searchable|string|false|none|Whether the content of this field can be searched.|
|types|[string]|false|none|The data types of items in the field.|
|value|string|false|none|The field identifier.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|auto|true|
|auto|false|
|deprecated|true|
|deprecated|false|
|orderable|true|
|orderable|false|
|searchable|true|
|searchable|false|

A clause that asserts a previous value of a field. For example, `status WAS "Resolved" BY currentUser() BEFORE "2019/02/02"`. See [WAS](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/dgiiLQ#Advancedsearching-operatorsreference-WASWAS) for more information about the WAS operator.

|operator|string|true|none|The operator between the field and operand.|
|predicates|[[JqlQueryClauseTimePredicate](#schemajqlqueryclausetimepredicate)]|true|none|The list of time predicates.|

|Property|Value|

|operator|was not|

Details about a filter.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string|false|none|A description of the filter.|
|editPermissions|[[SharePermission](#schemasharepermission)]|false|none|The groups and projects that can edit the filter.|
|favourite|boolean|false|none|Whether the filter is selected as a favorite.|
|favouritedCount|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The count of how many users have selected this filter as a favorite, including the filter owner.|
|id|string|false|read-only|The unique identifier for the filter.|
|jql|string|false|none|The JQL query for the filter. For example, *project = SSP AND issuetype = Bug*.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the filter. Must be unique.|
|owner|object|false|read-only|The user who owns the filter. This is defaulted to the creator of the filter, however Jira administrators can change the owner of a shared filter in the admin settings.|
|searchUrl|string(uri)|false|read-only|A URL to view the filter results in Jira, using the [Search for issues using JQL](#api-rest-api-3-filter-search-get) operation with the filter's JQL string to return the filter results. For example, *https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/search?jql=project+%3D+SSP+AND+issuetype+%3D+Bug*.|
|self|string(uri)|false|read-only|The URL of the filter.|
|sharePermissions|[[SharePermission](#schemasharepermission)]|false|none|The groups and projects that the filter is shared with.|
|sharedUsers|object|false|read-only|A paginated list of the users that the filter is shared with. This includes users that are members of the groups or can browse the projects that the filter is shared with.|
|subscriptions|object|false|read-only|A paginated list of the users that are subscribed to the filter.|
|viewUrl|string(uri)|false|read-only|A URL to view the filter results in Jira, using the ID of the filter. For example, *https://your-domain.atlassian.net/issues/?filter=10100*.|

Details of a filter.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string|false|none|The description of the filter.|
|editPermissions|[[SharePermission](#schemasharepermission)]|false|none|The groups and projects that can edit the filter. This can be specified when updating a filter, but not when creating a filter.|
|expand|string|false|read-only|Expand options that include additional filter details in the response.|
|favourite|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the filter is selected as a favorite by any users, not including the filter owner.|
|favouritedCount|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The count of how many users have selected this filter as a favorite, including the filter owner.|
|id|string|false|read-only|The unique identifier for the filter.|
|jql|string|false|read-only|The JQL query for the filter. For example, *project = SSP AND issuetype = Bug*.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the filter.|
|owner|object|false|read-only|The user who owns the filter. Defaults to the creator of the filter, however, Jira administrators can change the owner of a shared filter in the admin settings.|
|searchUrl|string(uri)|false|read-only|A URL to view the filter results in Jira, using the [Search for issues using JQL](#api-rest-api-3-filter-search-get) operation with the filter's JQL string to return the filter results. For example, *https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/search?jql=project+%3D+SSP+AND+issuetype+%3D+Bug*.|
|self|string(uri)|false|read-only|The URL of the filter.|
|sharePermissions|[[SharePermission](#schemasharepermission)]|false|none|The groups and projects that the filter is shared with. This can be specified when updating a filter, but not when creating a filter.|
|subscriptions|[[FilterSubscription](#schemafiltersubscription)]|false|read-only|The users that are subscribed to the filter.|
|viewUrl|string(uri)|false|read-only|A URL to view the filter results in Jira, using the ID of the filter. For example, *https://your-domain.atlassian.net/issues/?filter=10100*.|

### Properties

If not set, the status icon doesn't display a tooltip in Jira.<br> *  For the remote object icon it is used in conjunction with the application name to display a tooltip for the link's icon. The tooltip takes the format "\[application name\] icon title". Blank itemsare excluded from the tooltip title. If both items are blank, the icon tooltop displays as "Web Link".|
|url16x16|string|false|none|The URL of an icon that displays at 16x16 pixel in Jira.|

Details about an issue.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|changelog|object|false|read-only|Details of changelogs associated with the issue.|
|editmeta|object|false|read-only|The metadata for the fields on the issue that can be amended.|
|expand|string|false|read-only|Expand options that include additional issue details in the response.|
|fields|object|false|none|none|
|fieldsToInclude|[IncludedFields](#schemaincludedfields)|false|none|none|
|id|string|false|read-only|The ID of the issue.|
|key|string|false|read-only|The key of the issue.|
|names|object|false|read-only|The ID and name of each field present on the issue.|
|operations|object|false|read-only|The operations that can be performed on the issue.|
|properties|object|false|read-only|Details of the issue properties identified in the request.|
|renderedFields|object|false|read-only|The rendered value of each field present on the issue.|
|schema|object|false|read-only|The schema describing each field present on the issue.|
|self|string(uri)|false|read-only|The URL of the issue details.|
|transitions|[[IssueTransition](#schemaissuetransition)]|false|read-only|The transitions that can be performed on the issue.|
|versionedRepresentations|object|false|read-only|The versions of each field on the issue.|

<h2 id="tocS_IssueLinkType">IssueLinkType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaissuelinktype"></a>
<a id="schema_IssueLinkType"></a>
<a id="tocSissuelinktype"></a>
<a id="tocsissuelinktype"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "inward": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "outward": "string",
  "self": "http://example.com"
}
```

This object is used as follows:

 *  In the [ issueLink](#api-rest-api-3-issueLink-post) resource it defines and reports on the type of link between the issues. Find a list of issue link types with [Get issue link types](#api-rest-api-3-issueLinkType-get).
 *  In the [ issueLinkType](#api-rest-api-3-issueLinkType-post) resource it defines and reports on issue link types.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|The ID of the issue link type and is used as follows:<br><br> *  In the [ issueLink](#api-rest-api-3-issueLink-post) resource it is the type of issue link. Required on create when `name` isn't provided. Otherwise, read only.<br> *  In the [ issueLinkType](#api-rest-api-3-issueLinkType-post) resource it is read only.|
|inward|string|false|none|The description of the issue link type inward link and is used as follows:<br><br> *  In the [ issueLink](#api-rest-api-3-issueLink-post) resource it is read only.<br> *  In the [ issueLinkType](#api-rest-api-3-issueLinkType-post) resource it is required on create and optional on update. Otherwise, read only.|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the issue link type and is used as follows:<br><br> *  In the [ issueLink](#api-rest-api-3-issueLink-post) resource it is the type of issue link. Required on create when `id` isn't provided. Otherwise, read only.<br> *  In the [ issueLinkType](#api-rest-api-3-issueLinkType-post) resource it is required on create and optional on update. Otherwise, read only.|
|outward|string|false|none|The description of the issue link type outward link and is used as follows:<br><br> *  In the [ issueLink](#api-rest-api-3-issueLink-post) resource it is read only.<br> *  In the [ issueLinkType](#api-rest-api-3-issueLinkType-post) resource it is required on create and optional on update. Otherwise, read only.|
|self|string(uri)|false|read-only|The URL of the issue link type. Read only.|

```json
  "maxResults": 0,
  "query": "string",
  "startAt": 0,
  "validation": "strict"
}
```

The JQL specifying the issues available in the evaluated Jira expression under the `issues` context variable. Not all issues returned by the JQL query are loaded, only those described by the `startAt` and `maxResults` properties. To determine whether it is necessary to iterate to ensure all the issues returned by the JQL query are evaluated, inspect `meta.issues.jql.count` in the response.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|maxResults|integer(int32)|false|none|The maximum number of issues to return from the JQL query. Inspect `meta.issues.jql.maxResults` in the response to ensure the maximum value has not been exceeded.|
|query|string|false|none|The JQL query.|
|startAt|integer(int64)|false|none|The index of the first issue to return from the JQL query.|
|validation|string|false|none|Determines how to validate the JQL query and treat the validation results.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|validation|strict|
|validation|warn|
|validation|none|

<h2 id="tocS_JiraExpressionComplexity">JiraExpressionComplexity</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemajiraexpressioncomplexity"></a>


Details about the complexity of the analysed Jira expression.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expensiveOperations|string|true|none|Information that can be used to determine how many [expensive operations](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/jira-expressions/#expensive-operations) the evaluation of the expression will perform. This information may be a formula or number. For example:<br><br> *  `issues.map(i => i.comments)` performs as many expensive operations as there are issues on the issues list. So this parameter returns `N`, where `N` is the size of issue list.<br> *  `new Issue(10010).comments` gets comments for one issue, so its complexity is `2` (`1` to retrieve issue 10010 from the database plus `1` to get its comments).|
|variables|object|false|none|Variables used in the formula, mapped to the parts of the expression they refer to.|

All the fields of the issue object are available in the Jira expression.<br> *  `json`: A JSON object containing custom content.<br> *  `list`: A JSON list of `user`, `issue`, or `json` variable types.|

### Properties

|*anyOf*|[CompoundClause](#schemacompoundclause)|false|none|A JQL query clause that consists of nested clauses. For example, `(labels in (urgent, blocker) OR lastCommentedBy = currentUser()). Note that, where nesting is not defined, the parser nests JQL clauses based on the operator precedence. For example, "A OR B AND C" is parsed as "(A OR B) AND C". See Setting the precedence of operators for more information about precedence in JQL queries.`|
|*anyOf*|[FieldValueClause](#schemafieldvalueclause)|false|none|A clause that asserts the current value of a field. For example, `summary ~ test`.|
|*anyOf*|[FieldWasClause](#schemafieldwasclause)|false|none|A clause that asserts a previous value of a field. For example, `status WAS "Resolved" BY currentUser() BEFORE "2019/02/02"`. See [WAS](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/dgiiLQ#Advancedsearching-operatorsreference-WASWAS) for more information about the WAS operator.|
|*anyOf*|[FieldChangedClause](#schemafieldchangedclause)|false|none|A clause that asserts whether a field was changed. For example, `status CHANGED AFTER startOfMonth(-1M)`.See [CHANGED](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/dgiiLQ#Advancedsearching-operatorsreference-CHANGEDCHANGED) for more information about the CHANGED operator.|

<h2 id="tocS_MultipleCustomFieldValuesUpdate">MultipleCustomFieldValuesUpdate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamultiplecustomfieldvaluesupdate"></a>

```json
{

    0
  ],
  "value": null
}
```

A custom field and its new value with a list of issue to update.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customField|string|true|write-only|The ID or key of the custom field. For example, `customfield_10010`.|
|issueIds|[integer(int64)]|true|write-only|The list of issue IDs.|
|value|object|true|none|The value for the custom field. The value must be compatible with the [custom field type](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/manifest-reference/modules/jira-custom-field/#data-types) as follows:<br><br> *  `string` the value must be a string.<br> *  `number` the value must be a number.<br> *  `datetime` the value must be a string that represents a date in the ISO format or the simplified extended ISO format. For example, `"2023-01-18T12:00:00-03:00"` or `"2023-01-18T12:00:00.000Z"`. However, the milliseconds part is ignored.<br> *  `user` the value must be an object that contains the `accountId` field.<br> *  `group` the value must be an object that contains the group `name` or `groupId` field. Because group names can change, we recommend using `groupId`.<br><br>A list of appropriate values must be provided if the field is of the `list` [collection type](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/manifest-reference/modules/jira-custom-field/#collection-types).|

|password|string|false|none|This property is no longer available. If the user has an Atlassian account, their password is not changed. If the user does not have an Atlassian account, they are sent an email asking them set up an account.|

<h2 id="tocS_OrderOfCustomFieldOptions">OrderOfCustomFieldOptions</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaorderofcustomfieldoptions"></a>
<a id="schema_OrderOfCustomFieldOptions"></a>
<a id="tocSorderofcustomfieldoptions"></a>
<a id="tocsorderofcustomfieldoptions"></a>

```json
{
  "after": "string",
  "customFieldOptionIds": [
    "string"
  ],
  "position": "First"
}
```

An ordered list of custom field option IDs and information on where to move them.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after|string|false|write-only|The ID of the custom field option or cascading option to place the moved options after. Required if `position` isn't provided.|
|customFieldOptionIds|[string]|true|write-only|A list of IDs of custom field options to move. The order of the custom field option IDs in the list is the order they are given after the move. The list must contain custom field options or cascading options, but not both.|
|position|string|false|write-only|The position the custom field options should be moved to. Required if `after` isn't provided.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|position|First|
|position|Last|

An ordered list of issue type IDs and information about where to move them.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after|string|false|write-only|The ID of the issue type to place the moved issue types after. Required if `position` isn't provided.|
|issueTypeIds|[string]|true|write-only|A list of the issue type IDs to move. The order of the issue type IDs in the list is the order they are given after the move.|
|position|string|false|write-only|The position the issue types should be moved to. Required if `after` isn't provided.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|position|First|
|position|Last|

This permission can be one of the built-in permissions or a custom permission added by an app. See [Built-in permissions](../api-group-permission-schemes/#built-in-permissions) in *Get all permission schemes* for more information about the built-in permissions. See the [project permission](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/modules/project-permission/) and [global permission](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/modules/global-permission/) module documentation for more information about custom permissions.|

Details about a project.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|archived|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the project is archived.|
|archivedBy|object|false|read-only|The user who archived the project.|
|archivedDate|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The date when the project was archived.|
|assigneeType|string|false|read-only|The default assignee when creating issues for this project.|
|avatarUrls|object|false|read-only|The URLs of the project's avatars.|
|components|[[ProjectComponent](#schemaprojectcomponent)]|false|read-only|List of the components contained in the project.|
|deleted|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the project is marked as deleted.|
|deletedBy|object|false|read-only|The user who marked the project as deleted.|
|deletedDate|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The date when the project was marked as deleted.|
|description|string|false|read-only|A brief description of the project.|
|email|string|false|none|An email address associated with the project.|
|expand|string|false|read-only|Expand options that include additional project details in the response.|
|favourite|boolean|false|none|Whether the project is selected as a favorite.|
|id|string|false|none|The ID of the project.|
|insight|object|false|read-only|Insights about the project.|
|isPrivate|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the project is private.|
|issueTypeHierarchy|object|false|read-only|The issue type hierarchy for the project.|
|issueTypes|[[IssueTypeDetails](#schemaissuetypedetails)]|false|read-only|List of the issue types available in the project.|
|key|string|false|read-only|The key of the project.|
|landingPageInfo|object|false|read-only|The project landing page info.|
|lead|object|false|read-only|The username of the project lead.|
|name|string|false|read-only|The name of the project.|
|permissions|object|false|read-only|User permissions on the project|
|projectCategory|object|false|read-only|The category the project belongs to.|
|projectTypeKey|string|false|read-only|The [project type](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/GwiiLQ#Jiraapplicationsoverview-Productfeaturesandprojecttypes) of the project.|
|properties|object|false|read-only|Map of project properties|
|retentionTillDate|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The date when the project is deleted permanently.|
|roles|object|false|read-only|The name and self URL for each role defined in the project. For more information, see [Create project role](#api-rest-api-3-role-post).|
|self|string(uri)|false|read-only|The URL of the project details.|
|simplified|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the project is simplified.|
|style|string|false|read-only|The type of the project.|
|url|string|false|read-only|A link to information about this project, such as project documentation.|
|uuid|string(uuid)|false|read-only|Unique ID for next-gen projects.|
|versions|[[Version](#schemaversion)]|false|read-only|The versions defined in the project. For more information, see [Create version](#api-rest-api-3-version-post).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|assigneeType|PROJECT_LEAD|
|assigneeType|UNASSIGNED|
|projectTypeKey|software|
|projectTypeKey|service_desk|
|projectTypeKey|business|
|style|classic|
|style|next-gen|

Details about a project component.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assignee|object|false|read-only|The details of the user associated with `assigneeType`, if any. See `realAssignee` for details of the user assigned to issues created with this component.|
|assigneeType|string|false|none|The nominal user type used to determine the assignee for issues created with this component. See `realAssigneeType` for details on how the type of the user, and hence the user, assigned to issues is determined. Can take the following values:<br><br> *  `PROJECT_LEAD` the assignee to any issues created with this component is nominally the lead for the project the component is in.<br> *  `COMPONENT_LEAD` the assignee to any issues created with this component is nominally the lead for the component.<br> *  `UNASSIGNED` an assignee is not set for issues created with this component.<br> *  `PROJECT_DEFAULT` the assignee to any issues created with this component is nominally the default assignee for the project that the component is in.<br><br>Default value: `PROJECT_DEFAULT`.  <br>Optional when creating or updating a component.|
|description|string|false|none|The description for the component. Optional when creating or updating a component.|
|id|string|false|read-only|The unique identifier for the component.|
|isAssigneeTypeValid|boolean|false|read-only|Whether a user is associated with `assigneeType`. For example, if the `assigneeType` is set to `COMPONENT_LEAD` but the component lead is not set, then `false` is returned.|
|lead|object|false|read-only|The user details for the component's lead user.|
|leadAccountId|string|false|write-only|The accountId of the component's lead user. The accountId uniquely identifies the user across all Atlassian products. For example, *5b10ac8d82e05b22cc7d4ef5*.|
|leadUserName|string|false|none|This property is no longer available and will be removed from the documentation soon. See the [deprecation notice](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/) for details.|
|name|string|false|none|The unique name for the component in the project. Required when creating a component. Optional when updating a component. The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|project|string|false|none|The key of the project the component is assigned to. Required when creating a component. Can't be updated.|
|projectId|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The ID of the project the component is assigned to.|
|realAssignee|object|false|read-only|The user assigned to issues created with this component, when `assigneeType` does not identify a valid assignee.|
|realAssigneeType|string|false|read-only|The type of the assignee that is assigned to issues created with this component, when an assignee cannot be set from the `assigneeType`. For example, `assigneeType` is set to `COMPONENT_LEAD` but no component lead is set. This property is set to one of the following values:<br><br> *  `PROJECT_LEAD` when `assigneeType` is `PROJECT_LEAD` and the project lead has permission to be assigned issues in the project that the component is in.<br> *  `COMPONENT_LEAD` when `assignee`Type is `COMPONENT_LEAD` and the component lead has permission to be assigned issues in the project that the component is in.<br> *  `UNASSIGNED` when `assigneeType` is `UNASSIGNED` and Jira is configured to allow unassigned issues.<br> *  `PROJECT_DEFAULT` when none of the preceding cases are true.|
|self|string(uri)|false|read-only|The URL of the component.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|assigneeType|PROJECT_DEFAULT|
|assigneeType|COMPONENT_LEAD|
|assigneeType|PROJECT_LEAD|
|assigneeType|UNASSIGNED|
|realAssigneeType|PROJECT_DEFAULT|
|realAssigneeType|COMPONENT_LEAD|
|realAssigneeType|PROJECT_LEAD|
|realAssigneeType|UNASSIGNED|

<h2 id="tocS_SearchRequestBean">SearchRequestBean</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasearchrequestbean"></a>
<a id="schema_SearchRequestBean"></a>
<a id="tocSsearchrequestbean"></a>
<a id="tocssearchrequestbean"></a>

```json
{
  "expand": [
    "string"
  ],
  "fields": [
    "string"
  ],
  "fieldsByKeys": true,
  "jql": "string",
  "maxResults": 50,
  "properties": [
    "string"
  ],
  "startAt": 0,
  "validateQuery": "strict"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expand|[string]|false|none|Use [expand](em>#expansion) to include additional information about issues in the response. Note that, unlike the majority of instances where `expand` is specified, `expand` is defined as a list of values. The expand options are:<br><br> *  `renderedFields` Returns field values rendered in HTML format.<br> *  `names` Returns the display name of each field.<br> *  `schema` Returns the schema describing a field type.<br> *  `transitions` Returns all possible transitions for the issue.<br> *  `operations` Returns all possible operations for the issue.<br> *  `editmeta` Returns information about how each field can be edited.<br> *  `changelog` Returns a list of recent updates to an issue, sorted by date, starting from the most recent.<br> *  `versionedRepresentations` Instead of `fields`, returns `versionedRepresentations` a JSON array containing each version of a field's value, with the highest numbered item representing the most recent version.|
|fields|[string]|false|none|A list of fields to return for each issue, use it to retrieve a subset of fields. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `*all` Returns all fields.<br> *  `*navigable` Returns navigable fields.<br> *  Any issue field, prefixed with a minus to exclude.<br><br>The default is `*navigable`.<br><br>Examples:<br><br> *  `summary,comment` Returns the summary and comments fields only.<br> *  `-description` Returns all navigable (default) fields except description.<br> *  `*all,-comment` Returns all fields except comments.<br><br>Multiple `fields` parameters can be included in a request.<br><br>Note: All navigable fields are returned by default. This differs from [GET issue](#api-rest-api-3-issue-issueIdOrKey-get) where the default is all fields.|
|fieldsByKeys|boolean|false|none|Reference fields by their key (rather than ID). The default is `false`.|
|jql|string|false|none|A [JQL](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/egORLQ) expression.|
|maxResults|integer(int32)|false|none|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|properties|[string]|false|none|A list of up to 5 issue properties to include in the results. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list.|
|startAt|integer(int32)|false|none|The index of the first item to return in the page of results (page offset). The base index is `0`.|
|validateQuery|string|false|none|Determines how to validate the JQL query and treat the validation results. Supported values:<br><br> *  `strict` Returns a 400 response code if any errors are found, along with a list of all errors (and warnings).<br> *  `warn` Returns all errors as warnings.<br> *  `none` No validation is performed.<br> *  `true` *Deprecated* A legacy synonym for `strict`.<br> *  `false` *Deprecated* A legacy synonym for `warn`.<br><br>The default is `strict`.<br><br>Note: If the JQL is not correctly formed a 400 response code is returned, regardless of the `validateQuery` value.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|validateQuery|strict|
|validateQuery|warn|
|validateQuery|none|
|validateQuery|true|
|validateQuery|false|

Details of a share permission for the filter.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|group|object|false|none|The group that the filter is shared with. For a request, specify the `groupId` or `name` property for the group. As a group's name can change, use of `groupId` is recommended.|
|id|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The unique identifier of the share permission.|
|project|object|false|none|The project that the filter is shared with. This is similar to the project object returned by [Get project](#api-rest-api-3-project-projectIdOrKey-get) but it contains a subset of the properties, which are: `self`, `id`, `key`, `assigneeType`, `name`, `roles`, `avatarUrls`, `projectType`, `simplified`.  <br>For a request, specify the `id` for the project.|
|role|object|false|none|The project role that the filter is shared with.  <br>For a request, specify the `id` for the role. You must also specify the `project` object and `id` for the project that the role is in.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of share permission:<br><br> *  `user` Shared with a user.<br> *  `group` Shared with a group. If set in a request, then specify `sharePermission.group` as well.<br> *  `project` Shared with a project. If set in a request, then specify `sharePermission.project` as well.<br> *  `projectRole` Share with a project role in a project. This value is not returned in responses. It is used in requests, where it needs to be specify with `projectId` and `projectRoleId`.<br> *  `global` Shared globally. If set in a request, no other `sharePermission` properties need to be specified.<br> *  `loggedin` Shared with all logged-in users. Note: This value is set in a request by specifying `authenticated` as the `type`.<br> *  `project-unknown` Shared with a project that the user does not have access to. Cannot be set in a request.|
|user|object|false|none|The user account ID that the filter is shared with. For a request, specify the `accountId` property for the user.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|user|
|type|group|
|type|project|
|type|projectRole|
|type|global|
|type|loggedin|
|type|authenticated|
|type|project-unknown|

```json
{
  "accountId": "string",
  "groupId": "string",
  "groupname": "string",
  "projectId": "string",
  "projectRoleId": "string",
  "rights": 0,
  "type": "user"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accountId|string|false|none|The user account ID that the filter is shared with. For a request, specify the `accountId` property for the user.|
|groupId|string|false|none|The ID of the group, which uniquely identifies the group across all Atlassian products.For example, *952d12c3-5b5b-4d04-bb32-44d383afc4b2*. Cannot be provided with `groupname`.|
|groupname|string|false|none|The name of the group to share the filter with. Set `type` to `group`. Please note that the name of a group is mutable, to reliably identify a group use `groupId`.|
|projectId|string|false|none|The ID of the project to share the filter with. Set `type` to `project`.|
|projectRoleId|string|false|none|The ID of the project role to share the filter with. Set `type` to `projectRole` and the `projectId` for the project that the role is in.|
|rights|integer(int32)|false|none|The rights for the share permission.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the share permission.Specify the type as follows:<br><br> *  `user` Share with a user.<br> *  `group` Share with a group. Specify `groupname` as well.<br> *  `project` Share with a project. Specify `projectId` as well.<br> *  `projectRole` Share with a project role in a project. Specify `projectId` and `projectRoleId` as well.<br> *  `global` Share globally, including anonymous users. If set, this type overrides all existing share permissions and must be deleted before any non-global share permissions is set.<br> *  `authenticated` Share with all logged-in users. This shows as `loggedin` in the response. If set, this type overrides all existing share permissions and must be deleted before any non-global share permissions is set.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|user|
|type|project|
|type|group|
|type|projectRole|
|type|global|
|type|authenticated|

<h2 id="tocS_User">User</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemauser"></a>
<a id="schema_User"></a>
<a id="tocSuser"></a>
<a id="tocsuser"></a>

```json
{
  "accountId": "string",
  "accountType": "atlassian",
  "active": true,
  "applicationRoles": {
    "callback": {},
    "items": [
      {
        "defaultGroups": [
          "string"
        ],
        "defaultGroupsDetails": [
          {
            "groupId": "string",
            "name": "string",
            "self": "http://example.com"
          }
        ],
        "defined": true,
        "groupDetails": [
          {
            "groupId": "string",
            "name": "string",
            "self": "http://example.com"
          }
        ],
        "groups": [
          "string"
        ],
        "hasUnlimitedSeats": true,
        "key": "string",
        "name": "string",
        "numberOfSeats": 0,
        "platform": true,
        "remainingSeats": 0,
        "selectedByDefault": true,
        "userCount": 0,
        "userCountDescription": "string"
      }
    ],
    "max-results": 0,
    "pagingCallback": {},
    "size": 0
  },
  "avatarUrls": {
    "16x16": "http://example.com",
    "24x24": "http://example.com",
    "32x32": "http://example.com",
    "48x48": "http://example.com"
  },
  "displayName": "string",
  "emailAddress": "string",
  "expand": "string",
  "groups": {
    "callback": {},
    "items": [
      {
        "groupId": "string",
        "name": "string",
        "self": "http://example.com"
      }
    ],
    "max-results": 0,
    "pagingCallback": {},
    "size": 0
  },
  "key": "string",
  "locale": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "self": "http://example.com",
  "timeZone": "string"
}
```

A user with details as permitted by the user's Atlassian Account privacy settings. However, be aware of these exceptions:

 *  User record deleted from Atlassian: This occurs as the result of a right to be forgotten request. In this case, `displayName` provides an indication and other parameters have default values or are blank (for example, email is blank).
 *  User record corrupted: This occurs as a results of events such as a server import and can only happen to deleted users. In this case, `accountId` returns *unknown* and all other parameters have fallback values.
 *  User record unavailable: This usually occurs due to an internal service outage. In this case, all parameters have fallback values.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accountId|string|false|none|The account ID of the user, which uniquely identifies the user across all Atlassian products. For example, *5b10ac8d82e05b22cc7d4ef5*. Required in requests.|
|accountType|string|false|read-only|The user account type. Can take the following values:<br><br> *  `atlassian` regular Atlassian user account<br> *  `app` system account used for Connect applications and OAuth to represent external systems<br> *  `customer` Jira Service Desk account representing an external service desk|
|active|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the user is active.|
|applicationRoles|object|false|read-only|The application roles the user is assigned to.|
|avatarUrls|object|false|read-only|The avatars of the user.|
|displayName|string|false|read-only|The display name of the user. Depending on the user’s privacy setting, this may return an alternative value.|
|emailAddress|string|false|read-only|The email address of the user. Depending on the user’s privacy setting, this may be returned as null.|
|expand|string|false|read-only|Expand options that include additional user details in the response.|
|groups|object|false|read-only|The groups that the user belongs to.|
|key|string|false|none|This property is no longer available and will be removed from the documentation soon. See the [deprecation notice](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/) for details.|
|locale|string|false|read-only|The locale of the user. Depending on the user’s privacy setting, this may be returned as null.|
|name|string|false|none|This property is no longer available and will be removed from the documentation soon. See the [deprecation notice](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/) for details.|
|self|string(uri)|false|read-only|The URL of the user.|
|timeZone|string|false|read-only|The time zone specified in the user's profile. Depending on the user’s privacy setting, this may be returned as null.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|accountType|atlassian|
|accountType|app|
|accountType|customer|
|accountType|unknown|

|description|string|false|none|The description of the version. Optional when creating or updating a version.|
|expand|string|false|none|Use [expand](em>#expansion) to include additional information about version in the response. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `operations` Returns the list of operations available for this version.<br> *  `issuesstatus` Returns the count of issues in this version for each of the status categories *to do*, *in progress*, *done*, and *unmapped*. The *unmapped* property contains a count of issues with a status other than *to do*, *in progress*, and *done*.<br><br>Optional for create and update.|
|id|string|false|read-only|The ID of the version.|
|issuesStatusForFixVersion|object|false|read-only|If the expand option `issuesstatus` is used, returns the count of issues in this version for each of the status categories *to do*, *in progress*, *done*, and *unmapped*. The *unmapped* property contains a count of issues with a status other than *to do*, *in progress*, and *done*.|
|moveUnfixedIssuesTo|string(uri)|false|none|The URL of the self link to the version to which all unfixed issues are moved when a version is released. Not applicable when creating a version. Optional when updating a version.|
|name|string|false|none|The unique name of the version. Required when creating a version. Optional when updating a version. The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|operations|[[SimpleLink](#schemasimplelink)]|false|read-only|If the expand option `operations` is used, returns the list of operations available for this version.|
|overdue|boolean|false|read-only|Indicates that the version is overdue.|
|project|string|false|none|Deprecated. Use `projectId`.|
|projectId|integer(int64)|false|none|The ID of the project to which this version is attached. Required when creating a version. Not applicable when updating a version.|
|releaseDate|string(date)|false|none|The release date of the version. Expressed in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-mm-dd). Optional when creating or updating a version.|
|released|boolean|false|none|Indicates that the version is released. If the version is released a request to release again is ignored. Not applicable when creating a version. Optional when updating a version.|
|self|string(uri)|false|read-only|The URL of the version.|
|startDate|string(date)|false|none|The start date of the version. Expressed in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-mm-dd). Optional when creating or updating a version.|
|userReleaseDate|string|false|read-only|The date on which work on this version is expected to finish, expressed in the instance's *Day/Month/Year Format* date format.|
|userStartDate|string|false|read-only|The date on which work on this version is expected to start, expressed in the instance's *Day/Month/Year Format* date format.|

Details about a workflow scheme.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|defaultWorkflow|string|false|none|The name of the default workflow for the workflow scheme. The default workflow has *All Unassigned Issue Types* assigned to it in Jira. If `defaultWorkflow` is not specified when creating a workflow scheme, it is set to *Jira Workflow (jira)*.|
|description|string|false|none|The description of the workflow scheme.|
|draft|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the workflow scheme is a draft or not.|
|id|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The ID of the workflow scheme.|
|issueTypeMappings|object|false|none|The issue type to workflow mappings, where each mapping is an issue type ID and workflow name pair. Note that an issue type can only be mapped to one workflow in a workflow scheme.|
|issueTypes|object|false|read-only|The issue types available in Jira.|
|lastModified|string|false|read-only|The date-time that the draft workflow scheme was last modified. A modification is a change to the issue type-project mappings only. This property does not apply to non-draft workflows.|
|lastModifiedUser|object|false|read-only|The user that last modified the draft workflow scheme. A modification is a change to the issue type-project mappings only. This property does not apply to non-draft workflows.|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the workflow scheme. The name must be unique. The maximum length is 255 characters. Required when creating a workflow scheme.|
|originalDefaultWorkflow|string|false|read-only|For draft workflow schemes, this property is the name of the default workflow for the original workflow scheme. The default workflow has *All Unassigned Issue Types* assigned to it in Jira.|
|originalIssueTypeMappings|object|false|read-only|For draft workflow schemes, this property is the issue type to workflow mappings for the original workflow scheme, where each mapping is an issue type ID and workflow name pair. Note that an issue type can only be mapped to one workflow in a workflow scheme.|
|self|string(uri)|false|read-only|none|
|updateDraftIfNeeded|boolean|false|none|Whether to create or update a draft workflow scheme when updating an active workflow scheme. An active workflow scheme is a workflow scheme that is used by at least one project. The following examples show how this property works:<br><br> *  Update an active workflow scheme with `updateDraftIfNeeded` set to `true`: If a draft workflow scheme exists, it is updated. Otherwise, a draft workflow scheme is created.<br> *  Update an active workflow scheme with `updateDraftIfNeeded` set to `false`: An error is returned, as active workflow schemes cannot be updated.<br> *  Update an inactive workflow scheme with `updateDraftIfNeeded` set to `true`: The workflow scheme is updated, as inactive workflow schemes do not require drafts to update.<br><br>Defaults to `false`.|

Details of a worklog.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|author|object|false|read-only|Details of the user who created the worklog.|
|comment|object|false|none|A comment about the worklog in [Atlassian Document Format](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/apis/document/structure/). Optional when creating or updating a worklog.|
|created|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The datetime on which the worklog was created.|
|id|string|false|read-only|The ID of the worklog record.|
|issueId|string|false|read-only|The ID of the issue this worklog is for.|
|properties|[[EntityProperty](#schemaentityproperty)]|false|none|Details of properties for the worklog. Optional when creating or updating a worklog.|
|self|string(uri)|false|read-only|The URL of the worklog item.|
|started|string(date-time)|false|none|The datetime on which the worklog effort was started. Required when creating a worklog. Optional when updating a worklog.|
|timeSpent|string|false|none|The time spent working on the issue as days (\#d), hours (\#h), or minutes (\#m or \#). Required when creating a worklog if `timeSpentSeconds` isn't provided. Optional when updating a worklog. Cannot be provided if `timeSpentSecond` is provided.|
|timeSpentSeconds|integer(int64)|false|none|The time in seconds spent working on the issue. Required when creating a worklog if `timeSpent` isn't provided. Optional when updating a worklog. Cannot be provided if `timeSpent` is provided.|
|updateAuthor|object|false|read-only|Details of the user who last updated the worklog.|
|updated|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The datetime on which the worklog was last updated.|
|visibility|object|false|none|Details about any restrictions in the visibility of the worklog. Optional when creating or updating a worklog.|
